title: Open planned lifecycle events with PENDING resources
why: The cross-service feed for EOL deadlines (EKS, RDS, RDS CA, and others). It gives at least 180 days of notice for major changes and 90 days for minor ones, and lists each affected ARN as PENDING or RESOLVED.
detect: health describe-events --region us-east-1 --filter eventTypeCategories=scheduledChange,eventStatusCodes=open,upcoming; keep events whose eventTypeCode matches AWS_*_PLANNED_LIFECYCLE_EVENT; then health describe-affected-entities --filter eventArns=<arn>,statusCodes=PENDING. For organizations: describe-events-for-organization / describe-affected-entities-for-organization. Severity = days until event startTime (treat startTime as the change date; endTime is optional).
api_cost_note: Free, but needs Business Support+, Enterprise or Unified Operations (legacy Business/Enterprise On-Ramp still work until moved), otherwise SubscriptionRequiredException. Global endpoint is active in us-east-1, with us-east-2 as passive. The org view must already be enabled; enabling it is a mutation.
false_positive_traps: Events stay open up to 4 years. Entity status can lag up to 72h. GovCloud and China get no PENDING/RESOLVED status. Some events carry no entity status at all. Lambda deprecation notices expire 90 days after deprecation.

title: Use DescribeServiceLifecycle as the authoritative date table
why: A single schema with END_OF_SUPPORT, BLOCK_RESOURCE_CREATE and BLOCK_RESOURCE_UPDATE dates, impactRisks (END_OF_SUPPORT, BILLING, AVAILABILITY) and recommendedVersion for Lambda, RDS, Aurora, EKS, OpenSearch, ElastiCache and more. Every version check below can join its inventory against it instead of hardcoding dates.
detect: health describe-service-lifecycle [--filter service=LAMBDA|RDS|EKS...] with nextToken pagination; fields serviceLifecycles[].{service,version,title,recommendedVersion,lifecycleEvents[].{lifecycleEventType,date,impactRisks,regions}}. Join on the engine/runtime/version strings found by the per-service checks. AVAILABILITY < BILLING < END_OF_SUPPORT in urgency.
api_cost_note: The docs say 'customers on AWS Support'; whether this needs the same plan gate as other Health APIs is unverified. maxResults range is inconsistent in the docs (1-20 vs 10-100).
false_positive_traps: New API: coverage per service and the exact version strings (e.g. 'python3.14' vs RDS major '8.0') need normalization. regions ['all'] vs a specific list.

title: Cross-check versions against the endoflife.date API
why: A free, unauthenticated, MIT-licensed fallback for accounts without Health API access. Covers 21 Amazon-tagged products plus upstream OS and language EOL.
detect: GET https://endoflife.date/api/v1/products/{slug} (or /releases/{cycle}, /releases/latest). Slugs: amazon-eks, aws-lambda, amazon-rds-mysql, amazon-rds-postgresql, amazon-rds-mariadb, amazon-aurora-mysql, amazon-aurora-postgresql, amazon-documentdb, amazon-elasticache-redis, amazon-elasticsearch, amazon-opensearch, amazon-glue, amazon-linux, amazon-mq-activemq, amazon-mq-rabbitmq, amazon-msk, amazon-neptune, amazon-corretto, amazon-cdk. Fields: isEol, eolFrom, isEoes, eoesFrom, isMaintained, latest.
api_cost_note: No auth and no documented limit; may return HTTP 429 with Retry-After. Cache responses.
false_positive_traps: Community-maintained and can lag or differ from AWS (OpenSearch extended-support dates conflicted between the two). For EKS, eolFrom equals the end of standard support (not a hard EOL) and eoesFrom the end of extended support. Prefer AWS APIs when they are available.

title: EKS cluster on a Kubernetes version in extended support
why: Extended support costs $0.60/cluster-hour instead of $0.10, an extra $0.50/h or about $365/month per cluster. Currently standard is 1.34-1.37 and extended is 1.31-1.33.
detect: eks list-clusters; eks describe-cluster -> cluster.version, cluster.upgradePolicy.supportType (STANDARD|EXTENDED); eks describe-cluster-versions -> clusterVersions[].{clusterVersion,status (STANDARD_SUPPORT|EXTENDED_SUPPORT),endOfStandardSupportDate,endOfExtendedSupportDate}. Flag status==EXTENDED_SUPPORT and supportType==EXTENDED. Warn when endOfStandardSupportDate < now+60d (next: 1.34 on 2026-12-02).
api_cost_note: Free, regional; loop over every region.
false_positive_traps: Extended support is enabled by default. A cluster with supportType=STANDARD is never billed for extended support but gets auto-upgraded at the end of standard support. Billing starts at 00:00 UTC on the end-of-standard date. Provisioned Control Plane tiers are a separate, version-independent charge.

title: EKS control plane about to be force-upgraded
why: After the end of extended support (1.31 ends 2026-11-26), EKS auto-upgrades the control plane at any time and without notice. Managed and self-managed nodes and add-ons stay behind, which causes skew and breakage, and auto-upgraded clusters cannot be rolled back.
detect: Same calls as eks-cluster-extended-support-billing; flag endOfExtendedSupportDate < now+90d, or (supportType==STANDARD and endOfStandardSupportDate < now+60d).
false_positive_traps: Dates given only as month and year are approximate. Create is blocked on the end-of-extended date even before the auto-upgrade happens.

title: EKS upgrade-readiness insights in ERROR or WARNING
why: EKS-managed checks for deprecated or removed Kubernetes APIs, kubelet/kube-proxy skew and add-on incompatibility block a safe upgrade off extended or EOL versions.
detect: eks list-insights --cluster-name X --filter categories=UPGRADE_READINESS,statuses=ERROR,WARNING,UNKNOWN; eks describe-insight --id for recommendations and affected resources. ROLLBACK_READINESS only exists within 7 days of an upgrade.
false_positive_traps: Insights evaluate only EKS-managed add-on versions. Self-managed or overridden add-ons are invisible to them. Deprecated-API usage is based on recent audit traffic.

title: EKS add-on not compatible with, or behind the default for, the cluster version
why: VPC CNI, CoreDNS, kube-proxy, EBS CSI and similar add-ons on old versions break after a control-plane upgrade or forced upgrade, and miss CVE fixes.
detect: eks list-addons; eks describe-addon -> addon.addonVersion, status, health.issues; eks describe-addon-versions --addon-name N --kubernetes-version <cluster.version> -> addons[].addonVersions[].compatibilities[].{clusterVersion,defaultVersion}. Flag when the installed version is not in the compatible list, or is older than the defaultVersion. For self-managed add-ons, read kube-system DaemonSet/Deployment images with a read-only Kubernetes client.
source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/kubernetes-versions.html (extended support patches CNI, kube-proxy, CoreDNS); API names from the EKS API reference (unverified in this session)
false_positive_traps: Versions intentionally pinned. Marketplace and community add-ons have their own compatibility rules.

title: EKS nodes on Amazon Linux 2 AMIs
why: EKS stopped publishing AL2 and AL2-accelerated AMIs on 2025-11-26 (1.32 was the last version with AL2), and AL2 itself reached EOL on 2026-06-30, so these nodes get no further patches and no AMIs for newer Kubernetes versions.
detect: eks list-nodegroups; eks describe-nodegroup -> nodegroup.amiType in (AL2_x86_64, AL2_x86_64_GPU, AL2_ARM_64). Self-managed nodes and launch templates: ec2 describe-images on node ImageIds, name like amazon-eks-node-* / amazon-eks-gpu-node-* (AL2) vs amazon-eks-node-al2023-*. Karpenter: read-only kubectl get ec2nodeclass -o jsonpath={.spec.amiFamily|amiSelectorTerms}.
false_positive_traps: amiType=CUSTOM needs the image inspected. Windows and Bottlerocket are unaffected. This EOS is independent of Kubernetes extended support, so extended support does not cover AL2 nodes.

title: Node kubelet behind the control plane, or a stale node AMI release
why: Nodes are never auto-upgraded with the control plane. Skew of 3 or more minor versions is unsupported, and old AMI releases miss kernel and containerd CVE fixes.
detect: eks describe-nodegroup -> version, releaseVersion; compare to cluster.version and to ssm get-parameter --name /aws/service/eks/optimized-ami/<k8s>/amazon-linux-2023/x86_64/standard/recommended/release_version (parameter path unverified). Kubernetes read-only: nodes[].status.nodeInfo.kubeletVersion. Flag minor skew >=1 (warn) or >=3 (high), and releaseVersion older than 60 days.
api_cost_note: SSM public parameters: free reads, with throttling.
false_positive_traps: Fargate pods only pick up a new kubelet after the pod is restarted. Auto Mode nodes update themselves. Hybrid nodes are managed by the customer.

title: RDS or Aurora database billed for RDS Extended Support
why: Extended Support is billed per vCPU-hour (doc examples: $0.100 in years 1-2 in N. Virginia, $0.200 in year 3 in Ohio), standbys included and with no RI discount. RDS MySQL 8.0 left standard support on 2026-07-31, PG 13 on 2026-02-28, and PG 14 leaves it in Feb 2027.
detect: rds describe-db-instances / describe-db-clusters -> Engine, EngineVersion, EngineLifecycleSupport (open-source-rds-extended-support | open-source-rds-extended-support-disabled); rds describe-db-major-engine-versions -> DBMajorEngineVersions[].SupportedEngineLifecycles[].{LifecycleSupportName,LifecycleSupportStartDate,LifecycleSupportEndDate}. Flag when the major version's standard end date < now and enrollment is not disabled. Cost = vCPU x rate x 730.
false_positive_traps: SupportedEngineLifecycles is absent for commercial engines (Oracle, SQL Server, Db2), and MariaDB has standard support only. Aurora uses its own dates (Aurora MySQL 3 standard end is 2028-04-30 in most doc copies, with one conflicting 2027 copy). Aurora Serverless v1 is not eligible. Exact rates vary by region and engine.

title: RDS major version near end of extended support, or with no extended support
why: At the end of extended support (e.g. MySQL 5.7 on 2027-02-28), or for MariaDB or disabled enrollment past the standard end date, RDS auto-upgrades the major version, which can break applications and cause downtime.
detect: Join instances and clusters with describe-db-major-engine-versions. Flag when the extended LifecycleSupportEndDate < now+120d, or when only open-source-rds-standard-support exists and its end < now+90d. Also rds describe-pending-maintenance-actions -> PendingMaintenanceActionDetails[].Action=='db-upgrade' with AutoAppliedAfterDate/ForcedApplyDate.
false_positive_traps: Read replicas and cross-region replicas count separately. Blue/green deployments in progress.

title: RDS minor engine version deprecated, or an upgrade is pending
why: Deprecated minors are auto-upgraded on AWS's schedule and stop receiving fixes.
detect: rds describe-db-engine-versions --engine E --engine-version V --include-all -> DBEngineVersions[].Status (available|deprecated); rds describe-pending-maintenance-actions (db-upgrade, system-update); instance AutoMinorVersionUpgrade=false. Trusted Advisor 'Amazon RDS engine minor version upgrade is required'.
false_positive_traps: Extended Support minor versions are named like 5.7.44-RDS.YYYYMMDD and look odd but are supported.

title: Database on an expired or expiring CA or server certificate
why: rds-ca-2019 expired in Aug 2024. Clients that verify TLS fail after the CA or server certificate expires, and AWS surfaces this as a planned lifecycle event.
detect: rds describe-db-instances -> CACertificateIdentifier, CertificateDetails.{CAIdentifier,ValidTill}; flag rds-ca-2019 or ValidTill < now+90d. rds describe-certificates for CA ValidTill. rds describe-pending-maintenance-actions -> Action in (ca-certificate-rotation, server-certificate-rotation). describe-db-engine-versions SupportsCertificateRotationWithoutRestart tells whether a reboot is needed. Same fields via docdb and neptune describe-db-instances.
false_positive_traps: Clients that do not verify certificates are unaffected. On engines that support it, the server certificate auto-rotates at half its life without a restart. RDS Proxy uses ACM certificates.

title: DocumentDB 3.6 cluster in paid extended support
why: 3.6 left standard support on 2026-03-30 and extended support runs to 2029-03-30, billed as a premium. AWS pages disagree on whether year-1 pricing started 2026-03-31 or 2026-07-01.
detect: docdb describe-db-clusters --filters Name=engine,Values=docdb -> EngineVersion startswith '3.6'; also describe-db-instances for the instance count.
api_cost_note: Free; the docdb CLI uses the RDS endpoint, so filter by engine.
false_positive_traps: No EOL is announced for 4.0 or 5.0. Elastic clusters are versioned differently.

title: Neptune engine version at or near end of life
why: At EOL Neptune auto-upgrades in the maintenance window and blocks new clusters, instances and autoscaling. 1.1.1.0 and every 1.2.x reach EOL on 2026-12-04; 1.3.x through 1.4.6.x on 2027-03-06; 1.4.6.2 through 1.4.7.1 on 2027-06-03.
detect: neptune describe-db-clusters --filters Name=engine,Values=neptune -> EngineVersion; compare with the EOL table (or neptune describe-db-engine-versions --engine neptune for what is still offered). Flag EOL < now+90d.
false_positive_traps: Neptune Analytics graphs are separate. At least 3 months of notice by email and Health.

title: ElastiCache Redis OSS 4, 5 or 6 in, or entering, paid extended support
why: Redis OSS v4 and v5 have been in extended support since 2026-02-01; the year-1 premium in the doc example is 80% of the on-demand node price and is not discounted by RIs. v6 leaves standard support on 2027-01-31. v4 and v5 are force-upgraded to Valkey after 2029-01-31.
detect: elasticache describe-replication-groups and describe-cache-clusters --show-cache-node-info -> Engine=='redis', EngineVersion major in {4,5,6}, CacheNodeType, node count; elasticache describe-serverless-caches -> Engine, MajorEngineVersion. Cost = node on-demand price x premium% x nodes x 730.
false_positive_traps: Valkey and Redis OSS 7.x are unaffected. Memcached has no extended-support schedule listed. The year-2 and year-3 premium percentages are unverified.

title: Unapplied ElastiCache service updates past the recommended apply date
why: Security patches not applied by their deadline may be applied automatically, or leave known CVEs open.
detect: elasticache describe-update-actions --service-update-status available --update-action-status not-applied,waiting-to-start,stopped -> ServiceUpdateSeverity (critical|important), ServiceUpdateRecommendedApplyByDate, SlaMet.
false_positive_traps: Low-severity updates that are optional.

title: OpenSearch or Elasticsearch domain on an extended-support engine
why: Since 2026-11-07 the extended-support surcharge equals the instance price (doubling compute cost) for ES 1.5-7.8 except 5.6, OpenSearch 1.0-1.2 and 2.3-2.9, with support through 2027-11-07. ES 5.6 stays at $0.0065 per normalized instance hour until 2028-11-07.
detect: opensearch list-domain-names; opensearch describe-domains --domain-names ... -> EngineVersion ('Elasticsearch_X.Y' | 'OpenSearch_X.Y'), ClusterConfig instance type and count. Flag versions in the lists above, and those announced for future end of standard support (ES 6.8, 7.9, 7.10; OS 1.3, 2.11-2.19). opensearch get-compatible-versions shows upgrade targets.
false_positive_traps: OpenSearch Serverless collections are unaffected. Storage is not surcharged. endoflife.date dates for this differed from the AWS docs.

title: OpenSearch service software update available or scheduled
why: Service software updates carry security fixes and get applied automatically on an AutomatedUpdateDate.
detect: opensearch describe-domains -> ServiceSoftwareOptions.{UpdateAvailable,UpdateStatus,AutomatedUpdateDate,OptionalDeployment}. Flag UpdateAvailable=true and OptionalDeployment=false.
false_positive_traps: Optional updates.

title: MSK cluster on a Kafka version past end of support
why: Past end of support, MSK auto-upgrades to the recommended version at any time and without notice. 3.6.0 ended 2026-06-01 and 3.7.x ended 2026-09-01; 3.8, 3.9 (recommended), 4.x have no end date yet.
detect: kafka list-clusters-v2 -> ClusterInfoList[].Provisioned.CurrentBrokerSoftwareInfo.KafkaVersion (Serverless has no version); kafka list-kafka-versions -> KafkaVersions[].{Version,Status}. Flag versions with an EOS date < now+90d, or Status=DEPRECATED.
false_positive_traps: 3.7.x and later auto-track patch versions, so a 3.7.x label alone does not mean unpatched. ZooKeeper vs KRaft mode matters when moving to 4.x.

title: Amazon MQ broker on an ActiveMQ or RabbitMQ version at or near end of support
why: Brokers are auto-upgraded in the maintenance window within 45 days after end of support, with at least 90 days of notice, and creates are blocked within 30 days of it.
detect: mq list-brokers; mq describe-broker -> EngineType, EngineVersion, AutoMinorVersionUpgrade, MaintenanceWindowStartTime; mq describe-broker-engine-types --engine-type ACTIVEMQ|RABBITMQ -> supported versions. Compare with the version support calendars.
false_positive_traps: Specific current EOS dates are unverified (doc snapshots conflicted). RabbitMQ 4.2 and ActiveMQ 5.19 appear to be the latest. AWS may end support without notice for quality or security reasons.

title: Redshift provisioned clusters on DC2 or DS2 nodes or a trailing track
why: DS2 is gone. DC2 retirement was announced in Apr 2025 (feature development stops and clusters move to a long-term maintenance track). The DC2 EOL date is unverified (2026-04-24 per a community post).
detect: redshift describe-clusters -> NodeType (dc2.*, ds2.*), ClusterVersion, MaintenanceTrackName, NumberOfNodes; redshift describe-cluster-tracks for available tracks.
false_positive_traps: Serverless workgroups have no node type. Official DC2 EOL date unverified.

title: Lambda function on a deprecated or soon-deprecated managed runtime
why: Deprecated runtimes get no patches or support. Create, then update, gets blocked: block-create 2027-07-29 and block-update 2027-08-31 for most deprecated runtimes. Recent deprecations: nodejs18.x (2025-09-01), python3.9 (2025-12-15), ruby3.2 (2026-03-31), nodejs20.x (2026-04-30), provided.al2 (2026-07-31), python3.10 (2026-10-31), dotnet8 (2026-11-10). Next: nodejs22.x 2027-05-30; python3.11, java8.al2, java11, java17 2027-06-30.
detect: lambda list-functions --function-version ALL -> Functions[].{FunctionArn,Runtime,PackageType,LastModified}; flag Runtime in deprecated table, or deprecation < now+180d. Layers: lambda list-layers / list-layer-versions -> CompatibleRuntimes. Prioritize with CloudWatch AWS/Lambda Invocations Sum over 14d per FunctionName. Trusted Advisor L4dfs2Q4C5.
api_cost_note: list-functions is free and paginated per region. CloudWatch GetMetricData is billed per metric requested (about $0.01 per 1,000 metrics, unverified).
false_positive_traps: PackageType=Image has no Runtime field and gets no deprecation notice. Customer-managed runtimes show Runtime 'custom'. Lambda Web Functions are not returned. Published versions are immutable. Email and Health list only $LATEST versions.

title: Lambda on an Amazon Linux 2-based runtime after AL2 EOL
why: AL2 reached EOL on 2026-06-30. python3.10, python3.11, java8.al2, java11, java17 and provided.al2 now get only critical and selected-important AL2 fixes until their deprecation. AL2023 variants exist (java8.al2023 and others).
detect: list-functions --function-version ALL -> Runtime in {python3.10, python3.11, java8.al2, java11, java17, provided.al2}.
false_positive_traps: Do not double-count functions already flagged as deprecated.

title: Container-image Lambda built from an old or deprecated base image
why: Lambda does not patch or notify for image functions, so rebuilding is the customer's job.
detect: list-functions -> PackageType=='Image'; lambda get-function -> Code.ImageUri / ResolvedImageUri; ecr describe-images -> imagePushedAt; flag images older than 90 days. Optionally inspect the image config for base-image labels.
api_cost_note: Free; ECR is cross-account when images come from another account.
false_positive_traps: Image age is a proxy for patch level; a recent push can still use an old base image.

title: Lambda@Edge association on a deprecated runtime
why: Edge functions follow Lambda runtime deprecation. Once update is blocked, the CloudFront behavior can no longer get new function versions.
detect: cloudfront list-distributions -> DefaultCacheBehavior and CacheBehaviors.Items[].LambdaFunctionAssociations.Items[].LambdaFunctionARN (versioned); lambda get-function-configuration --region us-east-1 --function-name <versioned ARN> -> Runtime; compare with the deprecated table.
source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/runtime-support-policy.html (runtime list); the Lambda@Edge runtime subset is unverified
api_cost_note: CloudFront API is global; Lambda@Edge source functions live in us-east-1.
false_positive_traps: CloudFront Functions (cloudfront-js-1.0/2.0) are a different product. Replicas linger after the association is removed.

title: Glue jobs on an end-of-life Glue or Python version
why: At EOL, jobs on that version cannot start and running ones are stopped. Glue 0.9, 1.0 and 2.0 (Spark) reached EOL on 2026-04-01; PythonShell 3.6 on 2026-06-01. Glue Ray jobs have been in maintenance since 2026-03-31.
detect: glue get-jobs -> Jobs[].{Name,GlueVersion,Command.Name (glueetl|gluestreaming|pythonshell|glueray),Command.PythonVersion}; flag GlueVersion in {0.9,1.0,2.0}, or pythonshell with PythonVersion 3 on Glue 1.0 (Python 3.6). Also glue get-dev-endpoints and glue list-sessions -> GlueVersion. Cross-check glue get-job-runs for recent failures.
false_positive_traps: For Python shell, GlueVersion does not affect the runtime; PythonVersion does. Jobs with no GlueVersion may default to a legacy version (unverified). Jobs not run in over a year are zombies, not outages.

title: EMR clusters, Serverless apps or EKS jobs on out-of-support releases
why: EMR 5.35 and older, and 6.5 and older, entered End of Support on 2026-09-01 (no fixes, no support cases; EOL from 2027-09-01, possibly removed from the API). 5.36 and 6.6-6.15 have extended support to 2027-06-30; 7.0-7.10 to 2027-08-31. EMR never auto-upgrades.
detect: emr list-clusters --active (plus --created-after for transient clusters) -> describe-cluster ReleaseLabel; emr-serverless list-applications -> releaseLabel; emr-containers list-virtual-clusters / list-job-runs -> releaseLabel. Compare with the lifecycle table.
api_cost_note: Free; list-clusters is throttled, so page with backoff.
false_positive_traps: Transient clusters launched by orchestrators show up only in the terminated history. Extended support for migrating releases requires opening a support ticket.

title: SageMaker notebook instance on an AL1 or AL2 platform identifier
why: AL2 notebook support ended 2026-06-30, and instances cannot be created or restarted from 2026-07-01. notebook-al2-v1 and v2 (JupyterLab 1 and 3) ended 2025-06-30. SageMaker attempts automatic migration to AL2023 from 2026-07-15.
detect: sagemaker list-notebook-instances; sagemaker describe-notebook-instance -> PlatformIdentifier in {notebook-al1-*, notebook-al2-v1, notebook-al2-v2, notebook-al2-v3}, NotebookInstanceStatus. Target: notebook-al2023-v1.
false_positive_traps: Stopped instances cost only EBS but cannot be restarted (zombie).

title: Use of SageMaker features in maintenance, sunset or shutdown
why: Debugger, Model Monitor, Clarify, Ground Truth, GeoSpatial, A2I, Role Manager and Studio Lab entered maintenance on 2026-06-30. Profiler is sunset (ends 2027-06-30). Ground Truth Plus shut down on 2026-06-30.
detect: sagemaker list-monitoring-schedules; list-labeling-jobs; list-flow-definitions / list-human-task-uis (A2I); describe-training-job -> DebugHookConfig, ProfilerConfig, ProfilerRuleConfigurations; list-processing-jobs filtered on Clarify images.
false_positive_traps: Maintenance has no shutdown date. Only sunset or shutdown requires action.

title: Endpoints or jobs on unsupported framework containers
why: Prebuilt framework images (PyTorch, TensorFlow and others) lose patches after the framework support window.
detect: sagemaker list-endpoints -> describe-endpoint-config -> describe-model -> PrimaryContainer.Image / Containers[].Image; parse the framework version from the ECR tag and compare with the prebuilt-container support policy.
source: unverified (SageMaker prebuilt container support policy page)
false_positive_traps: Custom images that reuse DLC tags.

title: Beanstalk environment on a deprecated or retired platform branch
why: Retired branches get no security updates or support, with a 90-day grace period for existing environments, after which EB API actions may break.
detect: elasticbeanstalk describe-environments -> PlatformArn, SolutionStackName; elasticbeanstalk describe-platform-version --platform-arn A -> PlatformDescription.{PlatformBranchLifecycleState (Supported|Beta|Deprecated|Retired),PlatformLifecycleState}; elasticbeanstalk list-platform-branches --filters Attribute=LifecycleState,Operator=in,Values=Deprecated,Retired. Also managed updates: describe-configuration-settings, namespace aws:elasticbeanstalk:managedactions ManagedActionsEnabled.
false_positive_traps: A non-latest platform version on a Supported branch is only medium severity. Legacy, non-branch solution stacks need name parsing.

title: ECS service or task pinned to an old Fargate platform version
why: The LATEST Linux version is 1.4.0 and Windows is 1.0.0. Old pinned versions miss features and fixes.
detect: ecs list-clusters / list-services / describe-services -> services[].{launchType,platformVersion,platformFamily}; ecs describe-tasks -> platformVersion. Flag Linux platformVersion not in {LATEST, 1.4.0}.
api_cost_note: Free; describe-services takes 10 services and describe-tasks 100 per call.
false_positive_traps: Capacity providers mean launchType may be empty, so check capacityProviderStrategy.

title: Fargate task retirement scheduled (platform revision patching)
why: Standalone, scheduled, Batch and Step Functions tasks are stopped and not replaced on or after the retirement date (default wait 7 days, configurable to 14).
detect: Health describe-events with eventTypeCodes=AWS_ECS_TASK_PATCHING_RETIREMENT and status open/upcoming -> describe-affected-entities (status Impaired or Resolved); ecs list-account-settings --name fargateTaskRetirementWaitPeriod --effective-settings.
api_cost_note: Health API needs a qualifying support plan.
false_positive_traps: Service tasks are replaced automatically; only standalone tasks are at real risk. EC2 event windows override the wait period.

title: ECS container instances on old or AL2-based ECS-optimized AMIs or old agents
why: AL2 reached EOL on 2026-06-30. Stale AMIs and agents miss CVE fixes.
detect: ecs list-container-instances / describe-container-instances -> ec2InstanceId, versionInfo.{agentVersion,dockerVersion}, agentUpdateStatus; ec2 describe-instances -> ImageId; ec2 describe-images -> Name (amzn2-ami-ecs-* = AL2), CreationDate; compare with ssm get-parameter --name /aws/service/ecs/optimized-ami/amazon-linux-2023/recommended/image_id. Also ASG launch template ImageId.
source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/eks-ami-deprecation-faqs.html (AL2 EOS 2026-06-30); ECS SSM parameter path unverified in this session
false_positive_traps: Custom AMIs. Bottlerocket ECS variants.

title: Instances or launch templates using deprecated, disabled or very old AMIs
why: Old AMIs carry unpatched packages. Public AMIs auto-deprecate 2 years after creation, and deregistered AMIs break ASG and launch template scale-outs.
detect: ec2 describe-instances -> distinct ImageId; ec2 describe-images --image-ids ... --include-deprecated --include-disabled -> CreationDate, DeprecationTime, State (available|disabled), missing = deregistered. Also describe-launch-template-versions --versions '$Default' '$Latest' -> LaunchTemplateData.ImageId, and autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups. Thresholds: DeprecationTime < now (high), CreationDate > 180d (medium). For owned AMIs, LastLaunchedTime shows unused ones.
api_cost_note: Free. Always pass --image-ids or --owners self; an unfiltered public describe-images is huge.
false_positive_traps: Launch templates using resolve:ssm: parameters. Instances patched in place via SSM Patch Manager. Shared AMIs that are deregistered return nothing.

title: EC2 instances running an end-of-life OS
why: No security patches. Amazon Linux 2 reached EOL on 2026-06-30. Trusted Advisor has checks for Windows Server EOS (Qsdfp3A4L4), Ubuntu LTS end of standard support (c1dfprch15) and SQL Server EOS.
detect: ssm describe-instance-information -> PlatformType, PlatformName, PlatformVersion (managed nodes); otherwise ec2 describe-images -> Name and PlatformDetails of the instance AMI (amzn2-*, amzn-ami-*, Windows_Server-2012-*, ubuntu-*-18.04/20.04). Cross-reference endoflife.date amazon-linux, ubuntu, windows-server, rhel. Trusted Advisor checks above.
api_cost_note: Free; TA API needs a qualifying plan.
false_positive_traps: Ubuntu Pro/ESM or RHEL ELS subscriptions extend support. The AMI name only reflects the OS at launch, not later in-place upgrades.

title: Instances on previous-generation instance types
why: Worse price/performance (often 20% or more), limited capacity, and they are the first candidates for retirement.
detect: ec2 describe-instance-types --filters Name=current-generation,Values=false -> set; ec2 describe-instances -> InstanceType in set (state running or stopped). Do the same for RDS DBInstanceClass, ElastiCache CacheNodeType and OpenSearch instance types against each service's previous-generation list.
source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ec2/latest/instancetypes/ec2-previous-generation-instances.html (page not readable this session; CurrentGeneration filter from the EC2 API, unverified)
false_positive_traps: Reserved Instances or license-bound workloads. Some old families (t2) are still widely used.

title: EC2 instances with scheduled retirement, reboot or maintenance
why: Degraded hardware means instance-retire stops or terminates the instance on the scheduled date.
detect: ec2 describe-instance-status --include-all-instances -> InstanceStatuses[].Events[].{Code (instance-retire|instance-stop|instance-reboot|system-reboot|system-maintenance),NotBefore,Description}. Health scheduledChange events for EC2.
false_positive_traps: Descriptions starting with '[Completed]' or '[Canceled]'.

title: gp2 (and standard/io1) volumes that could move to gp3/io2
why: gp3 costs about 20% less per GB than gp2 (us-east-1 $0.08 vs $0.10/GB-month, unverified) and includes 3000 IOPS and 125 MB/s.
detect: ec2 describe-volumes --filters Name=volume-type,Values=gp2 (also standard, io1) -> Size, Iops, Attachments. Savings = Size x (gp2 - gp3 price). Compute Optimizer EBS recommendations.
false_positive_traps: gp2 volumes over 1 TiB get 3 IOPS/GiB (up to 16000) and over 170 GiB higher throughput, so gp3 needs provisioned IOPS and throughput to match. AMI defaults recreate gp2 root volumes.

title: Managed nodes running an outdated SSM Agent
why: Old agents miss fixes and features, and patch and inventory may fail.
detect: ssm describe-instance-information -> AgentVersion, IsLatestVersion==false, PingStatus.
false_positive_traps: Hybrid (mi-) nodes. Agents pinned on purpose.

title: Auto Scaling groups still on launch configurations
why: Launch configurations are legacy: no newer instance types, and new accounts cannot create them (dates unverified).
detect: autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups -> LaunchConfigurationName present (vs LaunchTemplate or MixedInstancesPolicy); autoscaling describe-launch-configurations -> ImageId, InstanceType.
source: unverified (EC2 Auto Scaling launch configurations docs)
false_positive_traps: Elastic Beanstalk or old CloudFormation-managed ASGs.

title: CloudFront distributions allowing SSLv3, TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1
why: Weak protocols and ciphers fail PCI and similar compliance. Modern policies are TLSv1.2_2021, TLSv1.2_2025 and TLSv1.3_2025.
detect: cloudfront list-distributions -> ViewerCertificate.{MinimumProtocolVersion,CloudFrontDefaultCertificate,IAMCertificateId,ACMCertificateArn}; flag MinimumProtocolVersion in {SSLv3, TLSv1, TLSv1_2016, TLSv1.1_2016}. Origins: Origins.Items[].CustomOriginConfig.{OriginSslProtocols.Items contains SSLv3|TLSv1|TLSv1.1, OriginProtocolPolicy=='http-only'}.
false_positive_traps: With the default *.cloudfront.net certificate the policy cannot be raised (effective minimum TLSv1, unverified). Legacy clients may require it.

title: HTTPS/TLS listeners using policies that allow TLS 1.0 or 1.1
why: The CLI, CloudFormation and CDK default is still ELBSecurityPolicy-2016-08, which allows TLS 1.0. Recommended: ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-Res-PQ-2025-09.
detect: elbv2 describe-load-balancers -> describe-listeners -> Listeners[?Protocol in (HTTPS,TLS)].SslPolicy; flag ELBSecurityPolicy-2016-08, -TLS-1-1-2017-01, -FS-1-1-2019-08, -TLS13-1-1-*, -TLS13-1-0-*, -TLS-1-0-2015-04, -FS-2018-06. elbv2 describe-ssl-policies --names X -> SslProtocols. CLB: elb describe-load-balancer-policies -> Reference-Security-Policy attribute.
false_positive_traps: NLB TCP passthrough listeners have no policy. Some IoT and legacy clients need TLS 1.0. The PQ-named TLS13-1-0-PQ policy still allows TLS 1.0.

title: API Gateway APIs or custom domains on TLS_1_0
why: Regional and edge-optimized REST APIs default to TLS_1_0. Newer SecurityPolicy_TLS13_* policies (with PQ and FIPS variants) exist.
detect: apigateway get-domain-names -> items[].{domainName,securityPolicy,endpointConfiguration.types}; apigatewayv2 get-domain-names -> DomainNameConfigurations[].SecurityPolicy; apigateway get-rest-apis -> security policy field (name unverified) and disableExecuteApiEndpoint. Flag TLS_1_0.
api_cost_note: Free; get-rest-apis is limited to about 10 req/s per account (unverified).
false_positive_traps: Default execute-api endpoints that are disabled. Private APIs default to TLS_1_2.

title: OpenSearch domain endpoint allowing TLS 1.0
why: Weak TLS on the domain endpoint.
detect: opensearch describe-domains -> DomainEndpointOptions.{EnforceHTTPS,TLSSecurityPolicy}; flag Policy-Min-TLS-1-0-2019-07 or EnforceHTTPS=false.
false_positive_traps: VPC-only domains with controlled clients.

title: ACM certificates expiring, failing renewal, or not renewable
why: An expired certificate takes down HTTPS. Imported and IssueCertificate private certificates are never renewed. Public validity dropped to 198 days with renewal 45 days before expiry (Feb 2026), so renewals now happen about twice as often.
detect: acm list-certificates (per region, plus us-east-1 for CloudFront) -> CertificateSummaryList[].{CertificateArn,Type (AMAZON_ISSUED|IMPORTED|PRIVATE),NotAfter,RenewalEligibility,InUse,Status}; acm describe-certificate -> RenewalSummary.{RenewalStatus (PENDING_AUTO_RENEWAL|PENDING_VALIDATION|SUCCESS|FAILED),DomainValidationOptions[].ValidationMethod}. Flag NotAfter < now+45d and (Type=IMPORTED, RenewalEligibility=INELIGIBLE, RenewalStatus in PENDING_VALIDATION|FAILED, or EMAIL validation). CloudWatch AWS/CertificateManager DaysToExpiry.
false_positive_traps: Certificates with InUse=false are not eligible for renewal unless exported, so they can expire harmlessly (zombie). ACME-issued certificates are renewed by the ACME client. A DNS CNAME removed breaks auto-renewal.

title: Expiring or expired IAM server certificates (legacy certificate store)
why: IAM-stored certificates never auto-renew. They are typically used by CloudFront (Trusted Advisor N425c450f2) or old ELBs.
detect: iam list-server-certificates -> ServerCertificateMetadataList[].{ServerCertificateName,Expiration,Path}; flag Expiration < now+30d or already expired.
false_positive_traps: Expired and unused certificates are just clutter.

title: Long-lived IAM access keys not rotated or unused
why: Old static keys are the most common breach vector (CIS uses a 90-day rotation and 45-90 day unused threshold).
detect: iam generate-credential-report then iam get-credential-report (CSV, base64). Flag access_key_{1,2}_active=TRUE with access_key_{1,2}_last_rotated > 90d; access_key_N_last_used_date N/A or > 90d (zombie); root row (<root_account>) with active keys; additional_credentials_info for more than 2 keys (use list-access-keys / get-access-key-last-used). Service-specific credentials: iam list-service-specific-credentials.
api_cost_note: Free and global; the report regenerates at most every 4h.
false_positive_traps: Break-glass users. Keys rotated by automation (last_rotated is accurate). Password last-used data has a May 2018 gap.

title: Lightsail instances or databases on inactive blueprints or EOL engines
why: Lightsail images and DB engines (MySQL, PostgreSQL) follow OS and engine EOL without RDS-style extended support.
detect: lightsail get-instances -> blueprintId, blueprintName; lightsail get-blueprints --include-inactive -> isActive=false; lightsail get-relational-databases -> engine, engineVersion, relationalDatabaseBlueprintId vs get-relational-database-blueprints; compare with endoflife.date.
false_positive_traps: Blueprints go inactive when a newer one replaces them, without being EOL.

title: Resources in AWS services in sunset, full shutdown or maintenance
why: Coming full shutdowns: App Mesh 2026-09-30, WAF Classic, Proton, IoT Greengrass V1, FinSpace and Lookout for Equipment 2026-10-07, Pinpoint 2026-10-30, Infrastructure Composer 2026-12-07. Already shut down: Inspector Classic, IoT Events, IQ and Panorama (2026-05-20), Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL (2026-01-27), OpsWorks (2024-05-01), QLDB (2025-07-31), Elastic Transcoder (2025-11-13). Ending 2027: DevOps Guru, Managed Blockchain, WorkMail, RDS Custom for Oracle, WorkSpaces PCoIP, Pools and Thin Client, AMS Advanced.
detect: Cheap read-only list calls per region: waf list-web-acls / waf-regional list-web-acls; appmesh list-meshes; pinpoint get-apps; proton list-services; greengrass list-groups (V1); lookoutequipment list-models; finspace list-environments; devops-guru describe-resource-collection; managedblockchain list-networks; workmail list-organizations; inspector list-assessment-templates; kinesisanalytics list-applications (v1); rds describe-db-instances with custom-oracle engine. Alternative: ce get-cost-and-usage for the last 90 days grouped by SERVICE.
api_cost_note: List calls are free. Cost Explorer costs $0.01 per request (unverified this session). Shut-down endpoints may return errors or DNS failures.
false_positive_traps: Maintenance (Cloud9, CloudSearch, CodeCatalyst, S3 Select, App Runner, Audit Manager, CloudTrail Lake, Kendra, Q Business, Timestream LiveAnalytics, Simple AD, Cognito Sync) has no shutdown date, so it is info only. CodeCommit is not on the current maintenance list. An endpoint error is not usage.

title: Account on the Developer, Business or Enterprise On-Ramp support plan (discontinued 2027-01-01)
why: These plans end on 2027-01-01. Health API and Trusted Advisor API access then requires Business Support+ ($29/month minimum), Enterprise or Unified Operations, so lifecycle automation that relies on them will break.
detect: Probe: health describe-events --max-items 1 -> SubscriptionRequiredException means no API entitlement. Cost Explorer get-cost-and-usage grouped by SERVICE for 'AWS Support (Business|Developer)' line items (service names unverified). support describe-severity-levels also fails on Basic.
false_positive_traps: GovCloud keeps the old plans. Enterprise On-Ramp customers are auto-upgraded to Enterprise.

title: Extended Support charges actually being billed
why: Confirms what each extended-support finding really costs and catches resources the inventory checks missed (other regions or accounts).
detect: ce get-cost-and-usage --granularity MONTHLY --group-by Type=DIMENSION,Key=USAGE_TYPE, filtered on USAGE_TYPE containing 'ExtendedSupport' (exact usage-type strings per service unverified), split by SERVICE and LINKED_ACCOUNT. Or CUR 2.0 / Data Exports in Athena on line_item_usage_type LIKE '%ExtendedSupport%'. The Cloud Intelligence Dashboards include an 'Extended Support - Cost Projection' view.
api_cost_note: Cost Explorer API about $0.01 per paginated request (unverified); run it from the payer account; data lags about 24h.
false_positive_traps: Usage-type naming differs by service. RDS charges start the day after the end of standard support; ElastiCache charges the first day of the next month.

title: Read Trusted Advisor's lifecycle-related checks
why: Gives AWS-computed affected-resource lists for deprecated Lambda runtimes (L4dfs2Q4C5, flags runtimes within 180 days), Windows Server EOS (Qsdfp3A4L4), Ubuntu LTS EOS (c1dfprch15), SQL Server EOS, required RDS minor upgrades, outdated ENA drivers on NitroV4, and CloudFront IAM certificates (N425c450f2).
detect: trustedadvisor list-checks / list-recommendations (new API), or support describe-trusted-advisor-check-result --check-id <id> (legacy). Read flaggedResources and status.
api_cost_note: The API needs Business Support+, Enterprise or Unified Operations. The Trusted Advisor API is in a few regions (us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-2, eu-west-1 and others).
false_positive_traps: Deprecated check IDs return errors. IDs for the SQL Server, RDS minor-version and ENA checks are unverified.

title: DMS replication instances on an end-of-support engine version
why: Each DMS version reaches end of support 18 months after release and is then auto-upgraded regardless of the auto-upgrade setting. For 3.5.4: no new instances from 2027-01-31, EOL 2027-03-31.
detect: dms describe-replication-instances -> ReplicationInstances[].{EngineVersion,AutoMinorVersionUpgrade}; dms describe-engine-versions -> EngineVersions[].{Version,Lifecycle,ReleaseStatus,AutoUpgradeDate,DeprecationDate} (field names partly unverified). DMS Serverless: describe-replication-configs.
false_positive_traps: Idle instances whose tasks have ended (zombie rather than outdated).

title: MWAA environments on end-of-support Airflow versions
why: End of support blocks new environments and existing ones run at the customer's own risk. 2.4.3, 2.5.1 and 2.6.3 ended 2025-12-30. At least 180 days of notice.
detect: mwaa list-environments; mwaa get-environment --name N -> Environment.AirflowVersion; compare with the deprecated-versions table.
false_positive_traps: Full current table not verified.

title: Canaries on deprecated Synthetics runtimes
why: Deprecated runtimes stop getting fixes. syn-nodejs-puppeteer-5.2, 6.2 and 7.0 were deprecated 2025-10-01; Python Selenium 5.0 and 5.1 on 2026-02-03.
detect: synthetics describe-canaries -> Canaries[].{Name,RuntimeVersion,Status.State}; synthetics describe-runtime-versions -> RuntimeVersions[].{VersionName,DeprecationDate}; flag DeprecationDate < now+90d.
false_positive_traps: Stopped canaries.

service: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
title: Flink applications on unsupported runtimes
why: Flink 1.6, 1.8 and 1.11 apps were forced to READY on 2025-07-14 and 1.13 support ended 2025-10-16 (per a localized doc). 1.15 and 1.18 are unsupported upstream. Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL shut down 2026-01-27.
detect: kinesisanalyticsv2 list-applications -> ApplicationSummaries[].RuntimeEnvironment (FLINK-1_x, SQL-1_0, ZEPPELIN-FLINK-x); kinesisanalytics list-applications (v1 SQL).
false_positive_traps: AWS-side support status can differ from upstream.

title: CodeBuild projects on old curated images
why: Old images ship EOL OS versions and language runtimes.
detect: codebuild list-projects; codebuild batch-get-projects -> projects[].environment.{image,type}; flag aws/codebuild/standard:N.0 or amazonlinux2-* older than the current list in the docs.
false_positive_traps: Custom ECR images.

title: API calls made by end-of-support AWS SDKs or CLI versions
why: Old SDKs miss security fixes and new endpoint and TLS behavior (e.g. JS SDK v2 and Java SDK v1 end of support, dates unverified).
detect: cloudtrail lookup-events (last 90 days of management events) -> userAgent containing aws-sdk-nodejs/2., aws-sdk-java/1., aws-cli/1., old boto3/botocore; group by userIdentity.arn.
api_cost_note: lookup-events is limited to about 2 TPS per region and returns 50 events per page, so sample rather than scan everything.
false_positive_traps: User-agent strings can be customized. Console and service-originated calls.

title: Aurora Serverless v1 clusters
why: v1 reached end of life (2025-03-31, unverified). It is not eligible for RDS Extended Support.
detect: rds describe-db-clusters -> EngineMode=='serverless' (v2 uses provisioned mode with ServerlessV2ScalingConfiguration).
source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/extended-support-versions.html (not eligible for extended support); EOL date unverified
false_positive_traps: Probably already converted by AWS.

title: Spend in regions outside the allowlist (catch-all for regions nobody looks at)
why: Forgotten resources usually live in regions nobody opens. Any cost in a non-allowlisted region is almost always a zombie or a compromise.
detect: account:ListRegions(RegionOptStatusContains=[ENABLED,ENABLED_BY_DEFAULT]) to get the scan set. Then ce:GetCostAndUsage, GroupBy REGION + SERVICE, MONTHLY, last 3 months. Flag any region not in the allowlist with spend over $1/month, and any 'global' line that should not exist.
false_positive_traps: Global services bill under 'global' or us-east-1 (Route 53, CloudFront, IAM Access Analyzer) and Global Accelerator bills under us-west-2. Org-wide security services (GuardDuty, Config, CloudTrail) running on purpose in every region. Tax and support lines.
api_cost_note: Cost Explorer API is billed per request (about $0.01, unverified). Run it once per payer account, not per region.

title: Cross-region inventory of every resource in non-primary regions
why: Gives one list of resources in every enabled region, so the per-service checks below don't miss regions.
detect: Resource Explorer aggregator index plus resource-explorer-2:Search 'region:<r>' per region, or a Config aggregator with SelectAggregateResourceConfig. Count resources by type in each region not on the allowlist. Ignore AWS-created defaults (default VPC/SG/subnets/IGW/DHCP options, default KMS aliases).
false_positive_traps: Default VPC objects exist in every region and inflate counts. Resource Explorer does not cover every resource type.
api_cost_note: Resource Explorer is free (unverified). Config charges per configuration item recorded.

title: Instances stopped for a long time that still pay for EBS and EIPs
why: A stopped instance pays nothing for compute but keeps paying for its EBS volumes, any attached EIP or public IPv4, and snapshots. Stopped for months usually means forgotten.
detect: ec2:DescribeInstances, filter instance-state-name=stopped. Parse StateTransitionReason 'User initiated (YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss GMT)' for the stop date and flag over 30 days. Cross-check CloudTrail LookupEvents EventName=StopInstances (90-day window only). Cost = sum of BlockDeviceMappings volume GB x volume type price, plus EIPs.
false_positive_traps: DR pilot-light or warm-standby instances. Auto Scaling warm pools keep Stopped instances on purpose. Instance Scheduler stops them every night. Hibernated instances. 'Golden' build boxes or license-bound hosts (MAC or ENI tied).
api_cost_note: Describe calls are free. LookupEvents is free but throttled to about 2 TPS per region (unverified).

title: Running instances or ASGs with no real activity
why: You pay the full instance-hour for doing nothing. GPU instances can cost thousands per month.
detect: compute-optimizer:GetIdleRecommendations (resourceType Ec2Instance / AutoScalingGroup). Idle means peak CPU under 5% and network under 5 MB/day over 14 days, with extra GPU criteria for G/P instances. Fallback: CloudWatch AWS/EC2 CPUUtilization Maximum plus NetworkIn+NetworkOut Sum, daily period, over 14-30 days.
false_positive_traps: Bastion and jump hosts, license servers, domain controllers, low-traffic VPN/NAT instances, monthly or seasonal batch. Use a 90-day daily window to catch these.
api_cost_note: Compute Optimizer needs opt-in per account or org and is regional. CloudWatch GetMetricData is always billed and not in the free tier.

title: On-Demand Capacity Reservations with unused capacity
why: An open ODCR is billed at the On-Demand rate whether or not instances run in it.
detect: ec2:DescribeCapacityReservations State=active. Flag AvailableInstanceCount == TotalInstanceCount, or a high unused ratio, for more than 7 days. Check EndDateType=unlimited. CloudWatch AWS/EC2CapacityReservations UnusedCapacity / InstanceUtilization.
false_positive_traps: Reservations held on purpose for DR failover or a launch-day spike. Reservations tied to Savings Plans or zonal RIs.

title: Dedicated Hosts allocated with no instances
why: Dedicated Hosts bill per host-hour whether or not anything runs on them.
detect: ec2:DescribeHosts State=available. Flag Instances list empty, or AvailableCapacity == full, for more than 7 days.
false_positive_traps: BYOL compliance hosts kept for license affinity. Hosts in a host resource group used by License Manager.

title: Persistent Spot requests or Spot Fleets that keep relaunching forgotten capacity
why: When nobody owns them, persistent requests and maintain-type fleets keep relaunching instances after you terminate them by hand.
detect: ec2:DescribeSpotInstanceRequests Type=persistent State=open|active; ec2:DescribeSpotFleetRequests State=active Type=maintain; ec2:DescribeFleets. Join to the instances' CPU and network idle signal and to the CreateTime age.
false_positive_traps: Long-running CI runners and batch fleets that are idle between jobs.

title: Unattached (available) EBS volumes
why: Detached volumes keep paying per GB-month plus provisioned IOPS and throughput (io1/io2/gp3) with no consumer.
detect: ec2:DescribeVolumes Filter status=available. Age from CreateTime, plus CloudTrail DetachVolume (90-day window). Compute Optimizer flags a volume 'Unattached' when it had no attachment over 32 days.
false_positive_traps: Kubernetes PVs with reclaimPolicy=Retain (tags kubernetes.io/created-for/pvc/name). Data volumes detached during a migration window. Volumes kept as evidence after an incident (forensics hold).

title: Attached but idle EBS volumes (non-root)
why: Volumes nobody reads or writes, often provisioned-IOPS volumes that are paid for and never used.
detect: Compute Optimizer idle: fewer than 1 read/write op per day over 14-32 days, root volumes excluded. Fallback: AWS/EBS VolumeReadOps + VolumeWriteOps Sum, daily period.
false_positive_traps: Cold data disks read once a quarter. Database log volumes on standby nodes.

title: Snapshots whose source volume is gone and that no AMI or backup plan references
why: Orphan snapshots pile up for years (GB-month billed) once the volume or the backup tool that made them is deleted.
detect: ec2:DescribeSnapshots OwnerIds=self. Orphan = VolumeId not in DescribeVolumes (copied or imported snapshots show vol-ffffffff) AND SnapshotId not in any DescribeImages(Owners=self, IncludeDeprecated=true, IncludeDisabled=true) BlockDeviceMappings AND not managed by AWS Backup (aws:backup:source-resource tag or description) or DLM (aws:dlm:lifecycle-policy-id tag). Also flag StartTime older than N days. Use StorageTier to spot archive-tier snapshots.
false_positive_traps: Compliance or legal retention (the final backup of a decommissioned system). Snapshots shared to or copied into DR accounts and regions. Archive-tier snapshots have a 90-day minimum, so early deletion is still billed (unverified). Snapshot storage is incremental, so deleting one may free less than its full size.
api_cost_note: Free, regional, paginated. In large accounts, run DescribeImages before DescribeSnapshots.

title: Owned AMIs that have not launched anything in a long time
why: Each AMI pins its backing EBS snapshots, which you pay for indefinitely.
detect: ec2:DescribeImages Owners=self, read LastLaunchedTime (data since April 2017, appears about 24 hours after a launch). Flag absent or older than 180 days. Then ec2:DescribeImageReferences (instances, launch templates, SSM parameters, Image Builder recipes) must return nothing. Check DescribeImageAttribute launchPermission to see whether the AMI is shared.
false_positive_traps: AMIs shared to other accounts (their launches may not show in your view, unverified). Legacy Launch Configurations are not in DescribeImageReferences, so check DescribeLaunchConfigurations too. DR AMIs copied to another region. Rollback or golden AMIs kept on purpose.

title: Elastic IPs not associated with anything
why: An idle EIP costs $0.005/hour (about $3.65/month) and advertises an address you may later release, which can leave dangling DNS.
detect: ec2:DescribeAddresses where AssociationId is absent. Also flag EIPs associated with a stopped instance's ENI, which is still billed as in-use. Trusted Advisor check 'Unassociated Elastic IP Addresses'.
false_positive_traps: IPs allowlisted by partners or customer firewalls, kept for a planned re-creation. BYOIP addresses are not charged.
api_cost_note: Free, regional. The Trusted Advisor API requires a Business or higher support plan.

title: All public IPv4 addresses, including auto-assigned ones on idle resources
why: Since 2024-02-01 every public IPv4 costs $0.005/hour whether in use or not (EC2, ELB, NAT, GA, Site-to-Site VPN, RDS public), so idle resources also pay for their IPs.
detect: VPC IPAM Public IP Insights (free tier), or ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces where Association.PublicIp is present, grouped by InterfaceType and RequesterId. Join to the idle checks for the owning resource. Cost and Usage Report line 'PublicIPv4:InUseAddress' / 'IdleAddress' (unverified usage-type names).
false_positive_traps: The EC2 Free Tier covers 750 hours/month of in-use IPv4 in the first 12 months, but idle addresses are not covered.

title: NAT gateways with no traffic or no route table pointing at them
why: A zonal NAT gateway costs $0.045/hour (about $33/month) plus its public IPv4. A regional NAT gateway bills per AZ.
detect: compute-optimizer:GetIdleRecommendations (NAT Gateway). Idle means available state, no route table association, zero ActiveConnectionCount and zero packets over 32 days. Fallback: ec2:DescribeRouteTables for routes with NatGatewayId, plus AWS/NATGateway BytesOutToDestination + BytesInFromSource Sum = 0 over 30 days.
false_positive_traps: A per-AZ backup NAT that is only routed during an AZ failover. A NAT used only by a monthly patch or batch window, so use 35+ days.
api_cost_note: GetMetricData is billed. Compute Optimizer is free (enhanced metrics are paid, unverified).

title: Load balancers with no traffic, no listeners or no healthy targets
why: Every ALB, NLB and CLB pays an hourly fee plus a public IPv4 per AZ, even at zero requests.
detect: elbv2:DescribeLoadBalancers / elb:DescribeLoadBalancers. Over 14-30 days: ALB AWS/ApplicationELB RequestCount Sum = 0; NLB AWS/NetworkELB NewFlowCount Sum = 0; CLB AWS/ELB RequestCount = 0. Also flag DescribeListeners empty, or every target group with zero healthy targets (DescribeTargetHealth). Trusted Advisor check 'Idle Load Balancers'.
false_positive_traps: DR standby stacks. Admin or rarely used internal endpoints. LBs behind Global Accelerator or CloudFront that only serve during failover. Ingress-controller-managed LBs: deleting by hand fights the controller.

title: Target groups with no load balancer or no registered targets
why: Mostly clutter that hides real configuration drift, and it counts toward the target group quota.
detect: elbv2:DescribeTargetGroups where LoadBalancerArns is empty, or DescribeTargetHealth returns zero targets, older than 30 days (no CreatedTime, so use the CloudTrail CreateTargetGroup event or IaC state).
false_positive_traps: Blue/green (CodeDeploy, ECS) keeps the idle colour's target group empty on purpose. Target groups used by Lambda targets, or pre-created for a planned cutover.

title: Network interfaces in 'available' state
why: Leaked ENIs use up subnet IPs, can block subnet or SG deletion, and cost IPv4 if they hold a public IP or EIP.
detect: ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces status=available. Exclude RequesterManaged=true unless the owning service resource is gone (Lambda Hyperplane, EFS, VPC endpoint, ELB). Flag 'aws-K8S-*' descriptions (VPC CNI leaks) and any with Association.PublicIp.
false_positive_traps: Secondary ENIs moved between instances for HA or licence MAC binding. Lambda VPC ENIs can stay 'available' for a while after a config change and are reclaimed by AWS.

title: DB instances or clusters with no connections
why: Idle database instances are among the largest zombie costs (instance-hours plus storage, IOPS and backups).
detect: compute-optimizer:GetIdleRecommendations (RDS/Aurora MySQL+PostgreSQL: no connections, low CPU, low IOPS). Fallback for every engine: AWS/RDS DatabaseConnections Maximum = 0 plus ReadIOPS/WriteIOPS near 0, daily period, over 14-30 days (90 days for seasonal). Aurora Serverless v2: ServerlessDatabaseCapacity pinned at MinCapacity with zero connections.
false_positive_traps: Read replicas and Aurora Global Database secondaries (excluded by Compute Optimizer). Clients connecting through RDS Proxy show connections on the proxy, not the instance. DR or warm standby. Month-end or year-end reporting databases.

title: Instances stopped long-term (auto-restarted every 7 days)
why: A stopped RDS instance still pays for storage and backups, and RDS starts it again on its own after 7 days, so compute bills silently resume.
detect: rds:DescribeDBInstances / DescribeDBClusters Status=stopped. rds:DescribeEvents for a recurring RDS-EVENT-0154 (auto-start after 7 days) followed by a stop, which shows a script that keeps re-stopping a database nobody uses.
false_positive_traps: Dev databases on a stop/start schedule that are used during working hours.
api_cost_note: DescribeEvents only covers the last 14 days (unverified), so poll on a schedule.

title: Old manual DB snapshots, including ones whose source is deleted
why: Manual snapshots never expire and are billed for backup storage beyond the free allowance.
detect: rds:DescribeDBSnapshots SnapshotType=manual and DescribeDBClusterSnapshots SnapshotType=manual. Flag SnapshotCreateTime older than N days, or a DBInstanceIdentifier that no longer exists. Include snapshots copied cross-region.
false_positive_traps: Final snapshots kept for compliance (often 7+ years). Snapshots shared to other accounts.

title: Provisioned clusters with no queries, paused clusters, and stale snapshots
why: Provisioned nodes bill per hour. A paused cluster drops compute charges but keeps paying for storage.
detect: redshift:DescribeClusters. Over 14-30 days: AWS/Redshift DatabaseConnections Max = 0 and CPUUtilization flat. Query SYS_QUERY_HISTORY / STL_QUERY for the last user query. Flag ClusterStatus=paused for more than 30 days. redshift:DescribeClusterSnapshots SnapshotType=manual with an old age. Serverless: sys_serverless_usage charged_seconds = 0.
false_positive_traps: A datashare producer serving consumers. Nightly or weekly ETL only, so use a window longer than the ETL period. A Serverless session left open in a transaction keeps consuming RPUs.
api_cost_note: GetMetricData is billed. Querying system tables needs database access (Data API).

title: EMR clusters WAITING/idle or with no auto-termination policy
why: An EMR cluster left in WAITING bills EC2 plus the EMR uplift for every node, around the clock.
detect: emr:ListClusters ClusterStates=[RUNNING,WAITING], read Status.Timeline.CreationDateTime. emr:GetAutoTerminationPolicy (absent means flag). Metrics: AWS/ElasticMapReduce IsIdle = 1 sustained over 1h+, or AutoTerminationClusterIdle. Flag WAITING for more than 1 hour, or age over 7 days on non-long-running clusters.
false_positive_traps: Long-running HBase, Presto/Trino or streaming clusters. IsIdle stays stuck at 1 for Zeppelin or Livy sessions after jobs finish, and only reflects YARN activity, so it misses non-YARN workloads.

title: Real-time inference endpoints with no invocations
why: Real-time endpoints bill per instance-hour (often GPU) while nobody calls them.
detect: sagemaker:ListEndpoints StatusEquals=InService. Compute Optimizer idle (SageMaker endpoints added 2026-06). AWS/SageMaker Invocations Sum = 0 per EndpointName+VariantName over 14-30 days. Instance count from DescribeEndpoint ProductionVariants CurrentInstanceCount.
false_positive_traps: Serverless endpoints and inference components that scale to zero (no idle cost). Async endpoints with MinCapacity=0. Endpoints for demos or batch scoring that run monthly.

title: Classic notebook instances left InService
why: Notebook instances bill per hour until stopped. GPU notebooks left on over weekends are a classic leak.
detect: sagemaker:ListNotebookInstances StatusEquals=InService. Flag LastModifiedTime older than 1 day, a missing lifecycle config with auto-stop, or a GPU instance type. Also flag Stopped notebooks with large VolumeSizeInGB that are old.
false_positive_traps: Users mid-experiment running long jobs inside the notebook.

title: Studio apps or spaces running without idle shutdown
why: JupyterLab, Code Editor and KernelGateway apps bill per instance-hour while running. Canvas bills per session hour (unverified).
detect: sagemaker:ListApps (Status=InService, AppType, ResourceSpec.InstanceType). sagemaker:DescribeDomain / DescribeUserProfile / DescribeSpace: check AppLifecycleManagement.IdleSettings (LifecycleManagement=ENABLED, IdleTimeoutInMinutes 60-525600). Flag domains with no idle settings, and apps whose CreationTime is older than 24 hours.
false_positive_traps: Built-in idle shutdown needs SageMaker Distribution 2.0+ images and doesn't trigger while jobs are running. 'default' JupyterServer apps cost nothing (unverified).

title: Domains or serverless collections with no searches or indexing
why: Domains bill instance-hours and EBS around the clock. Serverless collections have a minimum OCU floor.
detect: opensearch:ListDomainNames / DescribeDomains. Over 30 days: AWS/ES SearchRate and IndexingRate Sum near 0 (dimensions DomainName+ClientId). For Serverless: aoss:ListCollections plus AWS/AOSS SearchRequestRate / IngestionRequestRate (unverified metric names).
false_positive_traps: Log or SIEM domains with low write rates. Domains kept for compliance search on rare audits. Cross-cluster replication followers.

title: Cache clusters with no connections or commands
why: Cache nodes bill per node-hour (memory-optimized nodes are expensive) whether or not anything uses them.
detect: Compute Optimizer idle (Redis/Valkey node-based and serverless, MemoryDB): no new connections, engine CPU under 1%, no hits, misses, gets or sets over 14 days. Memcached fallback: AWS/ElastiCache CurrConnections, CmdGet+CmdSet Sum = 0.
false_positive_traps: Global Datastore secondaries. Warm standby caches for DR. Memcached is not covered by Compute Optimizer.

title: Document or graph DB clusters with no connections
why: Instance-hours plus storage and IO with no clients.
detect: Compute Optimizer idle for DocumentDB (no connections over 14 days, available status; elastic clusters excluded). Neptune: AWS/Neptune (unverified) or the instance's DatabaseConnections / Gremlin+SPARQL request metrics Sum = 0 over 30 days.
false_positive_traps: Like RDS, these can only be stopped for 7 days. DR or global-cluster secondaries.

title: Provisioned tables or GSIs with consumed capacity far below provisioned
why: Provisioned RCU/WCU are billed hourly whether consumed or not, and per-GSI capacity is easy to forget.
detect: dynamodb:ListTables + DescribeTable (BillingModeSummary=PROVISIONED). Over 14-30 days compare AWS/DynamoDB ConsumedReadCapacityUnits / ConsumedWriteCapacityUnits (per table and per GSI) with ProvisionedRead/Write. Flag peak utilization under 10%, or zero consumption (Compute Optimizer idle, added 2026-06). Check application-autoscaling MinCapacity floors.
false_positive_traps: Autoscaling floors set on purpose before a known spike (sales events). Global table replicas in DR regions. Seasonal workloads. Reserved capacity already purchased.
api_cost_note: GetMetricData is billed, regional, per GSI.

title: Streams or shards with no records, idle enhanced fan-out consumers, idle MSK clusters
why: Provisioned shards bill per shard-hour (about $0.015, unverified) and enhanced fan-out consumers bill per hour. MSK brokers bill per broker-hour.
detect: kinesis:ListStreams / DescribeStreamSummary (StreamModeDetails, OpenShardCount). Over 14 days: AWS/Kinesis IncomingRecords and GetRecords.Records Sum = 0, or IncomingBytes per shard well under 1 MB/s capacity. ListStreamConsumers for EFO consumers with SubscribeToShard.RecordsDelivered = 0. MSK: kafka:ListClustersV2 plus AWS/Kafka BytesInPerSec = 0.
false_positive_traps: Event streams that only carry traffic during incidents or replays. On-demand streams have an hourly base charge even when idle (unverified).

title: Interface or GWLB VPC endpoints processing no bytes
why: Interface endpoints bill per ENI per AZ per hour (about $0.01/hour in us-east-1). Ten services across three AZs is roughly $220/month.
detect: ec2:DescribeVpcEndpoints VpcEndpointType in [Interface, GatewayLoadBalancer, Resource]. AWS/PrivateLinkEndpoints BytesProcessed Sum = 0 over 30 days (dimensions VPC Endpoint Id, Service Name). Also flag endpoints in VPCs with zero non-endpoint ENIs.
false_positive_traps: SSM, SSM Messages and EC2 Messages endpoints only used during break-glass Session Manager access. DR VPCs. Gateway endpoints (S3, DynamoDB) are free and shouldn't be flagged.

title: Transit Gateway attachments with no traffic, or TGWs with no attachments
why: Each attachment bills hourly (about $0.05/attachment-hour per the AWS example), whether or not traffic flows.
detect: ec2:DescribeTransitGateways, DescribeTransitGatewayAttachments (State=available). Over 30 days: AWS/TransitGateway BytesIn + BytesOut per TransitGatewayAttachment Sum = 0. Also flag attachments to deleted or empty VPCs and stale peering attachments.
false_positive_traps: DR paths that are only active during failover. Inspection VPC attachments with low but non-zero traffic.
api_cost_note: GetMetricData is billed. The TGW may be owned by a network account via RAM.

service: Site-to-Site VPN / Client VPN / Direct Connect
title: VPN connections down or carrying no data, idle Client VPN associations, unused DX ports
why: A VPN connection bills hourly plus public IPv4 per tunnel. Client VPN bills per subnet association-hour. DX bills per port-hour.
detect: ec2:DescribeVpnConnections. Over 30 days: AWS/VPN TunnelState Max = 0 on both tunnels, or TunnelDataIn + TunnelDataOut Sum = 0. ec2:DescribeClientVpnEndpoints + DescribeClientVpnConnections (no connections over 30 days). directconnect:DescribeConnections + AWS/DX ConnectionBpsEgress/Ingress = 0, or ConnectionState down. Also flag orphan VGWs (no VPC attachment) and CGWs.
false_positive_traps: Backup VPN behind a primary DX (idle by design). Seasonal partner integrations.

title: Hosted zones that get no queries or are not delegated
why: Each zone bills monthly (about $0.50, unverified). An undelegated or abandoned public zone is also a delegation hygiene risk.
detect: route53:ListHostedZones. Public zones: AWS/Route53 DNSQueries (us-east-1 only, HostedZoneId dimension) Sum = 0 over 30 days. Resolve the parent NS with an external DNS lookup and compare it to GetHostedZone DelegationSet; a mismatch means the zone is not authoritative. Private zones: check VPCs from GetHostedZone still exist. Zones with only SOA/NS records.
false_positive_traps: Defensive or parked brand domains. Zones that only hold ACM DNS-validation CNAMEs, queried only at renewal. Private zones have no DNSQueries metric. Resolver query logs are the alternative.
api_cost_note: DNS query metrics are free. The Route 53 API is global with a low request rate limit (unverified).

title: Dangling DNS records pointing at deleted AWS resources (subdomain takeover)
why: An attacker can claim the deleted target (S3 bucket name, Elastic Beanstalk CNAME, released EIP, CloudFront alternate domain) and serve content or phish from your subdomain. AWS CIRT has seen attackers actively scanning for these.
detect: For every route53:ListResourceRecordSets record: CNAME or alias to *.s3*.amazonaws.com / s3-website: s3:HeadBucket on the bucket name (404 NoSuchBucket = critical). *.elasticbeanstalk.com: elasticbeanstalk:CheckDNSAvailability true means anyone can claim it (critical). *.cloudfront.net: the distribution must exist in the org and list the alias in Aliases. A/AAAA records with IPs in AWS ip-ranges.json that are not in any org account's DescribeAddresses or ENIs = released EIP (high). ELB, API Gateway or AppRunner names that no longer resolve. NS delegations to deleted hosted zones or to deleted subdomains. Optionally an AWS Config custom rule.
false_positive_traps: Records pointing to resources in another account or org you don't scan, such as partner SaaS or third-party CNAMEs (Heroku, Azure, GitHub Pages) that need provider-specific checks. ELB DNS names have a random component, so takeover risk is low. Wildcard records.
api_cost_note: S3 HeadBucket and CheckDNSAvailability are cheap or free. External DNS resolution needs no AWS API. The Route 53 API is global.

title: Distributions whose S3 origin bucket was deleted (origin takeover), and disabled or unused distributions
why: If the origin bucket name is free, an attacker can create it and your distribution serves their content under your domain. Disabled distributions still hold alternate domain names.
detect: cloudfront:ListDistributions, then for each S3 origin domain run s3:HeadBucket (404 = critical). Flag Enabled=false for more than 90 days. AWS/CloudFront Requests (us-east-1, Region=Global) Sum = 0 over 30 days.
false_positive_traps: OAC/OAI-protected origins reduce the exposure but don't remove the dangling configuration. Distributions kept as failover origins.

title: Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints with no queries or no rules
why: Each endpoint ENI costs $0.125/hour and you need at least two, so at least about $182/month per endpoint.
detect: route53resolver:ListResolverEndpoints plus ListResolverRules / ListResolverRuleAssociations (an outbound endpoint with no associated rules is a zombie). CloudWatch AWS/Route53Resolver InboundQueryVolume / OutboundQueryVolume Sum = 0 over 30 days (unverified metric names).
false_positive_traps: Hybrid DNS that is only used during on-premises failover.

title: Registered domains auto-renewing with no hosted zone or no traffic
why: An annual renewal fee for domains nobody uses. Letting a domain lapse is itself a takeover and phishing risk.
detect: route53domains:ListDomains (us-east-1), AutoRenew=true. Join to a hosted zone with DNSQueries = 0, or to no hosted zone at all.
false_positive_traps: Defensive or typo-squat brand registrations. Keep these rather than letting them lapse.

title: Incomplete multipart uploads with no abort lifecycle rule
why: Parts from failed uploads are billed as storage forever, and they don't show in normal object listings.
detect: S3 Storage Lens free metric IncompleteMPUStorageBytesOlderThan7Days (and IncompleteMultipartUploadStorageBytes) per bucket. Confirm with s3:ListMultipartUploads (Initiated date). s3:GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration missing AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload means flag.
false_positive_traps: Very large uploads in progress for days (backup appliances). Use 7+ days as the threshold.
api_cost_note: Storage Lens free metrics are kept 14 days. ListMultipartUploads is a LIST request (billed per 1,000).

title: Buckets nobody reads or writes
why: Abandoned buckets keep paying for storage, and they are often the forgotten home of public or sensitive data.
detect: S3 has no last-access API. Signals: Storage Lens advanced activity metrics (GetRequests, PutRequests; paid), CloudWatch request metrics with a filter (paid), CloudTrail S3 data events (paid), server access logs. BucketSizeBytes/NumberOfObjects (AWS/S3, daily, free) flat for 90+ days. IAM action-level last accessed for S3 actions on the roles that can reach the bucket.
false_positive_traps: Archive or Glacier buckets (low access by design). Log destination buckets (CloudTrail, ELB, VPC flow) that only AWS writes to. Object Lock or compliance buckets. Static website buckets served via CloudFront (requests hit CloudFront's cache).
api_cost_note: Free signals are weak. Strong signals (data events, advanced Storage Lens) are paid.

title: Versioned buckets with no noncurrent-version expiration
why: Every overwrite or delete keeps a billed noncurrent copy forever, so storage grows silently.
detect: s3:GetBucketVersioning Status=Enabled AND GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration without NoncurrentVersionExpiration or ExpiredObjectDeleteMarker. Size via Storage Lens noncurrent version storage bytes (free tier status unverified).
false_positive_traps: Buckets where versions are the recovery mechanism (ransomware protection), or under Object Lock retention.
api_cost_note: Bucket configuration GETs are cheap requests.

title: Log groups set to 'Never expire', plus orphan log groups of deleted resources
why: Log groups default to keeping data forever, billed per GB-month (about $0.03/GB archived in the us-east-1 examples). Orphan /aws/lambda/<deleted> groups pile up.
detect: logs:DescribeLogGroups where retentionInDays is absent, ordered by storedBytes. Orphans: /aws/lambda/<fn> where lambda:GetFunction returns 404, and the same idea for /aws/rds, /aws/eks, /aws/codebuild. No new data: AWS/Logs IncomingBytes Sum = 0 over 90 days, or DescribeLogStreams orderBy=LastEventTime.
false_positive_traps: Audit or security logs that must be kept (PCI, SOX, local data-protection law). Log groups whose data is exported or subscribed elsewhere (check DescribeSubscriptionFilters).
api_cost_note: DescribeLogGroups is free with a moderate TPS limit, regional.

title: Alarms stuck in INSUFFICIENT_DATA that watch deleted resources
why: Each standard alarm costs $0.10/month, and orphan alarms create noise that hides real ones.
detect: cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms StateValue=INSUFFICIENT_DATA with StateUpdatedTimestamp older than 30 days. Parse Dimensions (InstanceId, LoadBalancer, DBInstanceIdentifier) and check the resource still exists.
false_positive_traps: Alarms on sparse metrics (error counts that only appear on failure) with TreatMissingData=notBreaching.
api_cost_note: DescribeAlarms is free within API free-tier limits, regional.

title: Repositories with no lifecycle policy and images never pulled
why: Image storage grows without bound (about $0.10/GB-month, unverified), and old vulnerable images stay available to pull.
detect: ecr:DescribeRepositories. ecr:GetLifecyclePolicy returning LifecyclePolicyNotFoundException means flag. ecr:DescribeImages: imagePushedAt older than 90 days AND lastRecordedPullTime absent or older than 90 days (refreshed at least every 24 hours, so approximate). Untagged images count.
false_positive_traps: Images pinned by digest in production that are rarely re-pulled (long-lived nodes cache them). Lambda container images may not show recent pulls. Rollback images. Re-tagging does not update imagePushedAt.
api_cost_note: Free, regional. Replicated repositories exist in each replica region.

title: Customer managed keys with no cryptographic use
why: Each CMK costs $1/month, prorated hourly, plus $1/month for each of its first two rotations, and disabled keys are still billed. The bigger risk is deleting a key that still protects archived data.
detect: kms:ListKeys + DescribeKey (KeyManager=CUSTOMER, KeyState). kms:GetKeyLastUsage: if KeyLastUsage is absent and TrackingStartDate is earlier than now-90d, the key is a candidate. Confirm in CloudTrail (Decrypt/Encrypt/GenerateDataKey for the key ARN; data older than 90 days needs a trail or Lake) and review grants (ListGrants) and key policy.
false_positive_traps: Keys protecting rarely read data (S3 archives, EBS/RDS snapshots, backups, Secrets) where deletion means permanent data loss. Multi-Region replicas. Recommend disabling the key plus a CloudWatch alarm on use before scheduling deletion. Keys pending deletion are not billed.
api_cost_note: KMS API calls are billed per 10k (unverified). GetKeyLastUsage is regional.

title: Secrets not retrieved in 90+ days
why: Each secret costs $0.40/month, and stale credentials widen the attack surface.
detect: secretsmanager:ListSecrets, read LastAccessedDate (day precision; flag older than 90 days or absent with CreatedDate older than 90 days). AWS Config managed rule secretsmanager-secret-unused (unusedForDays default 90). Also check replica regions (ReplicationStatus).
false_positive_traps: Break-glass or DR credentials. Secrets read only at deploy time or by an annual job. Whether rotation Lambdas update LastAccessedDate is unverified. Secrets managed by RDS (ManagedRDS) are tied to the database.
api_cost_note: ListSecrets is billed as API calls (per 10k, unverified), regional.

title: IAM users with no console or key activity
why: Dormant users with credentials are a top initial-access vector, and they often belong to people who left.
detect: iam:GenerateCredentialReport + GetCredentialReport: password_last_used, access_key_1/2_last_used_date, mfa_active. Flag no activity over 90 days, console users without MFA, and users with both a password and keys. IAM Access Analyzer unused access analyzer covers unused passwords and keys.
false_positive_traps: Emergency break-glass users (should be monitored, not deleted). Service users for legacy on-premises integrations that authenticate rarely.
api_cost_note: Global and free. The Access Analyzer unused access analyzer costs $0.20 per role or user per month, and one analyzer covers all regions.

title: Access keys never used, or unused for 90+ days, or old active keys
why: A leaked long-lived key that nobody uses goes unnoticed until it is abused.
detect: iam:ListAccessKeys + GetAccessKeyLastUsed (LastUsedDate, ServiceName, Region). Flag a null LastUsedDate with CreateDate older than 7 days, LastUsedDate older than 90 days, or an Active key older than 90 days. The same keys show up in the credential report.
false_positive_traps: Keys for quarterly or annual jobs (audit exports, DR drills).
api_cost_note: Global and free. Throttles on IAM APIs mean you should use the credential report for large accounts.

title: Roles not assumed within the tracking window
why: Unused roles with broad trust or permissions are latent privilege-escalation paths.
detect: iam:GetRole RoleLastUsed.LastUsedDate/Region (trailing 400-day window). iam:GenerateServiceLastAccessedDetails + GetServiceLastAccessedDetails for service- and action-level unused permissions. IAM Access Analyzer unused access findings (UnusedIAMRole, UnusedPermission).
false_positive_traps: Service-linked roles (can't or shouldn't be deleted). DR, break-glass and incident-response roles. StackSets execution roles used only on deploy. Roles used only via iam:PassRole, which is not tracked. Regions that started tracking recently report a shorter window.
api_cost_note: Global and free. Access Analyzer costs $0.20 per role or user per month.

title: Unattached customer policies, unused SAML/OIDC providers, expired server certificates
why: Clutter that hides real permissions. An OIDC provider for a deleted CI/CD system or EKS cluster is a trust path nobody watches.
