detect: iam:ListPolicies Scope=Local OnlyAttached=false with AttachmentCount=0. iam:ListOpenIDConnectProviders / ListSAMLProviders: check whether any role's trust policy references them, and whether the EKS cluster for an oidc.eks.* issuer still exists. iam:ListServerCertificates with Expiration in the past.
false_positive_traps: Policies staged for future use or for permission boundaries. Providers used by roles in another account (not possible for OIDC trust, but check SCP or IaC references).

title: Functions never or rarely invoked, and idle provisioned concurrency
why: Idle functions cost almost nothing, except provisioned concurrency, which bills hourly. They do add attack surface (function URLs, old runtimes) and count toward the 75 GB code storage quota (unverified).
detect: lambda:ListFunctions (all versions). AWS/Lambda Invocations Sum = 0 over 90 days (daily period). lambda:ListProvisionedConcurrencyConfigs plus ProvisionedConcurrencyUtilization Max under 10%. ListFunctionUrlConfigs with AuthType=NONE on idle functions. Old versions via ListVersionsByFunction.
false_positive_traps: CloudFormation custom-resource handlers (invoked only on stack updates). Cognito or Config triggers, DR failover handlers, yearly cron jobs. Lambda@Edge replicas are cleaned up by CloudFront.
api_cost_note: GetMetricData is billed, regional (Lambda@Edge is us-east-1).

title: Failed, rolled-back or long-untouched stacks, and StackSet instances in unused regions
why: Failed stacks leave partially created, billable resources. Stale stacks show resources nobody owns.
detect: cloudformation:ListStacks StackStatusFilter in [ROLLBACK_COMPLETE, ROLLBACK_FAILED, DELETE_FAILED, CREATE_FAILED, UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED, REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS]. LastUpdatedTime older than 1 year. DetectStackDrift for stacks whose resources were deleted outside CloudFormation. ListStackSets + ListStackInstances for regions on no allowlist.
false_positive_traps: CDKToolkit bootstrap stacks, Control Tower, landing-zone and security baseline stacks: rarely updated, critical, don't touch.

title: Environments with no traffic, and terminated environments' CNAMEs
why: Each environment runs EC2, an ELB and EIPs. After termination, its *.elasticbeanstalk.com CNAME can be claimed by anyone if DNS still points there.
detect: elasticbeanstalk:DescribeEnvironments (Status=Ready, Health). The environment ELB's RequestCount Sum = 0 over 30 days, or DescribeEnvironmentHealth. For terminated environments (IncludeDeleted=true), check Route 53 for CNAMEs to the old EnvironmentCNAME (see route53-dangling-dns-takeover).
false_positive_traps: Worker-tier environments driven by SQS have no ELB requests, so check SQS NumberOfMessagesReceived instead.

title: WorkSpaces with no user connection in 63+ days
why: AlwaysOn WorkSpaces bill monthly per desktop. AutoStop ones still pay a monthly base fee (unverified).
detect: Compute Optimizer idle (AlwaysOn only, no connection over 63 days). workspaces:DescribeWorkspacesConnectionStatus LastKnownUserConnectionTimestamp. DescribeWorkspaces RunningMode.
false_positive_traps: Employees on leave. Seasonal contractors. Shared kiosk or test desktops.

title: Lightsail instances, static IPs, disks, snapshots, LBs and DBs nobody uses
why: Lightsail sits outside the normal EC2 consoles. A static IP left unattached for more than an hour costs $0.005/hour and often sits in a region nobody uses. Stopped instances still bill (unverified).
detect: In every Lightsail region: lightsail:GetInstances (state), GetStaticIps (isAttached=false), GetDisks (isAttached=false), GetInstanceSnapshots / GetDiskSnapshots (age), GetLoadBalancers, GetRelationalDatabases, GetContainerServices, GetBuckets, GetDistributions. Metrics via GetInstanceMetricData NetworkIn/CPUUtilization.
false_positive_traps: Lightsail databases auto-start after 7 days like RDS. Small personal sites with genuinely low traffic.
api_cost_note: Free. Lightsail regions are a subset of EC2 regions.

title: Managed AD / AD Connector / Simple AD with no consumers
why: Directories bill per hour per domain controller and can run hundreds of dollars a month.
detect: ds:DescribeDirectories. Look for consumers: workspaces:DescribeWorkspaceDirectories, RDS/FSx/QuickSight/IAM Identity Center/Connect references, ds:DescribeTrusts. No consumers and no domain-joined instances means zombie. Shared directories: DescribeSharedDirectories.
false_positive_traps: A directory backing IAM Identity Center or Windows EC2 domain join (not visible as an AWS-service consumer). Trusts to on-premises AD.

title: Accelerators with no flows, including disabled ones
why: Each accelerator has a fixed fee of $0.025/hour (about $18/month), charged even when disabled, until it is deleted.
detect: globalaccelerator:ListAccelerators (API only in us-west-2; Enabled flag). CloudWatch (us-west-2) AWS/GlobalAccelerator NewFlowCount and ProcessedBytesIn Sum = 0 over 30 days. Endpoint groups with no healthy endpoints.
false_positive_traps: Accelerators kept for their static anycast IPs that customers allowlist.

title: File systems with no reads or writes, and old backups
why: FSx bills for provisioned storage, throughput capacity and SSD IOPS whether used or not.
detect: fsx:DescribeFileSystems. Over 30 days: AWS/FSx DataReadBytes + DataWriteBytes Sum near 0 (plus ClientConnections where available). fsx:DescribeBackups older than retention with the file system deleted. Persistent Lustre scratch left after an HPC job.
false_positive_traps: ONTAP SnapMirror DR destinations. Windows file shares used only at month-end close.

title: EFS file systems with no mount targets or client connections
why: Storage is billed per GB-month, and provisioned throughput is billed whether or not anyone mounts the file system.
detect: efs:DescribeFileSystems (NumberOfMountTargets, SizeInBytes, ThroughputMode). NumberOfMountTargets=0, or AWS/EFS ClientConnections Sum = 0 over 30 days. DescribeReplicationConfigurations.
false_positive_traps: Replication destinations are read-only with no clients by design. File systems used by Lambda or Fargate only occasionally. Lifecycle-to-IA archives.

title: Leftover Cloud9 environments and their EC2/EBS
why: Cloud9 closed to new customers on 2024-07-25. Leftover environments keep EC2 instances and EBS volumes (aws-cloud9-* names), often with auto-hibernate disabled.
detect: cloud9:ListEnvironments + DescribeEnvironments (in every region). ec2:DescribeInstances with tag aws:cloud9:environment (unverified tag key) or Name aws-cloud9-*. Check the auto-stop setting. Flag stopped instances older than 30 days.
false_positive_traps: Existing customers still actively using it.

title: Stale parameters, especially advanced-tier ones
why: Advanced parameters bill monthly (about $0.05 each, unverified). Stale parameters also hold outdated AMI IDs, endpoints or secrets.
detect: ssm:DescribeParameters (Tier, LastModifiedDate, Type=SecureString). There is no last-read field, so use CloudTrail GetParameter/GetParameters/GetParametersByPath events (90-day window) for usage. Check ec2:DescribeImageReferences for parameters referencing deregistered AMIs.
false_positive_traps: Configuration read only at deploy or boot. CloudFormation dynamic references resolved only on stack updates.
api_cost_note: DescribeParameters is free (standard throughput limits), regional.

title: Security groups attached to no ENI and referenced by nothing
why: Unused permissive groups get reattached by mistake later. Stale cross-VPC references hide broken rules.
detect: ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups minus every GroupId in DescribeNetworkInterfaces Groups. Also exclude groups referenced by other rules (DescribeSecurityGroupRules ReferencedGroupInfo), launch templates/configurations, and Lambda/ECS/EMR/RDS configurations. ec2:DescribeStaleSecurityGroups per VPC. Firewall Manager usage audit policies can automate this.
false_positive_traps: Default SGs (can't be deleted). Groups in launch templates of ASGs scaled to 0. Groups that EMR, Glue or Batch attach on demand. Groups referenced in IaC for future use.

title: Default VPCs in every enabled region, especially unused ones
why: Default VPCs have public subnets that auto-assign public IPs, so a launch in an unwatched region is internet-exposed and pays IPv4 charges.
detect: In every enabled region: ec2:DescribeVpcs Filter isDefault=true. Count ENIs in the VPC (DescribeNetworkInterfaces vpc-id). Zero ENIs means a deletion candidate. Also flag 'MapPublicIpOnLaunch=true' subnets.
false_positive_traps: Legacy workloads that live in the default VPC. Some services and tutorials assume a default VPC exists.

title: Unused or expired certificates, and idle Private CAs
why: Public ACM certs are free, but each AWS Private CA bills monthly (about $400 general-purpose, unverified). Expired imported certs signal dead services.
detect: acm:ListCertificates + DescribeCertificate: InUseBy empty, Status=EXPIRED, or imported with NotAfter in the past. acm-pca:ListCertificateAuthorities (Status=ACTIVE). A CA with no issuance (CloudTrail IssueCertificate over 90 days, or an audit report) is idle.
false_positive_traps: Certs pre-provisioned for a cutover. Root CAs that rarely issue by design (they only sign subordinates).
api_cost_note: Free describe calls, regional (CloudFront certs live in us-east-1).

title: Recovery points of deleted resources, or with 'always' retention
why: Backups of decommissioned resources are kept and billed until their lifecycle ends, which may be never.
detect: backup:ListBackupVaults, ListRecoveryPointsByBackupVault: ResourceArn no longer exists, CalculatedLifecycle.DeleteAt absent (never expires), CreationDate old. Also check ListBackupPlans for plans with no selections.
false_positive_traps: Vault Lock or compliance retention (can't be deleted). Final backups kept on purpose. Cross-account backup vaults.

title: EKS clusters with no nodes, and ECS clusters with idle capacity
why: An EKS control plane costs $0.10/hour, or $0.60/hour in extended support, with zero workloads. ECS EC2 capacity bills while running no tasks.
detect: eks:ListClusters, ListNodegroups, ListFargateProfiles. Zero nodes (node group desiredSize=0 and no Karpenter or self-managed nodes; check ec2 tag kubernetes.io/cluster/<name>) means zombie. ecs:ListClusters + DescribeClusters (registeredContainerInstancesCount > 0 and runningTasksCount = 0). Compute Optimizer idle for ECS Fargate services.
false_positive_traps: DR clusters scaled to zero. Clusters whose nodes are registered by Karpenter only on demand.

title: Provisioned Throughput with no invocations
why: Provisioned model units bill hourly (often thousands per month) whether or not the model is called.
detect: bedrock:ListProvisionedModelThroughputs (status InService, commitmentDuration). AWS/Bedrock Invocations for the provisioned model ARN Sum = 0 over 7-14 days.
false_positive_traps: A commitment term already purchased can't be cancelled, so report it but no saving is available. Custom models that need Provisioned Throughput for occasional evaluation.

title: Hourly-billed managed endpoints with no work
why: DMS replication instances, Transfer Family servers (about $0.30/hour, unverified) and Network Firewall endpoints (about $0.395/hour per AZ, unverified) bill around the clock.
detect: dms:DescribeReplicationInstances with no running tasks (DescribeReplicationTasks Status). transfer:ListServers State=ONLINE plus AWS/Transfer BytesIn/BytesOut = 0 over 30 days. network-firewall:ListFirewalls plus AWS/NetworkFirewall Packets = 0, or no route table pointing at the firewall endpoints.
false_positive_traps: A DMS instance kept for CDC restarts. SFTP servers used by partners monthly.

title: Idle brokers, always-on streaming fleets, inactive BI users
why: Brokers and AppStream always-on instances bill hourly. QuickSight author and reader seats bill per user even when inactive (unverified).
detect: mq:ListBrokers plus AWS/AmazonMQ connection/message metrics = 0 over 30 days. appstream:DescribeFleets FleetType=ALWAYS_ON plus DescribeSessions (no sessions over 30 days). quicksight:ListUsers joined to CloudTrail or usage reports with no activity over 90 days.
false_positive_traps: Brokers used only for failover messaging. Seasonal training fleets.
api_cost_note: GetMetricData is billed, regional (QuickSight identity region).

title: Gateways offline or with no I/O, and orphaned gateway volumes/tapes
why: Gateway volume storage, virtual tapes (including archived ones) and EBS-snapshot-backed volumes keep billing after the on-premises appliance is gone.
detect: storagegateway:ListGateways + DescribeGatewayInformation (GatewayState, last software update). AWS/StorageGateway ReadBytes/WriteBytes = 0 over 30 days. ListVolumes / ListTapes / DescribeTapeArchives for a deleted or offline gateway. datasync:ListAgents Status=OFFLINE.
false_positive_traps: Archived tapes kept for regulatory retention.

title: Topics with no subscriptions, queues with no traffic, rules targeting deleted resources
why: Close to zero cost, but these are signs of dead integrations, and EventBridge rules pointing at deleted targets fail silently.
detect: sns:ListTopics + ListSubscriptionsByTopic (empty). AWS/SQS NumberOfMessagesSent + NumberOfMessagesReceived Sum = 0 over 90 days. events:ListRules + ListTargetsByRule where the target ARN no longer exists, plus AWS/Events FailedInvocations.
false_positive_traps: Alerting topics that are silent until an incident. Dead-letter queues are empty by design.

title: APIs or stages with no requests
why: Little direct cost (caching clusters are the exception: hourly), but they leave exposed endpoints and integrations to deleted backends.
detect: apigateway:GetRestApis + GetStages (cacheClusterEnabled). apigatewayv2:GetApis. AWS/ApiGateway Count Sum = 0 over 90 days per ApiName+Stage. Custom domain names (GetDomainNames) whose base-path mappings point to deleted APIs.
false_positive_traps: Webhook receivers called rarely. Private APIs used only during DR.

title: Alarm stuck in ALARM for days
why: A long-lived ALARM is either a real ongoing outage nobody acts on or a broken or noisy threshold that trains people to ignore alerts.
detect: cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms --state-value ALARM (metric and composite) per region; flag StateUpdatedTimestamp older than 3 days. Use DescribeAlarmHistory --history-item-type StateUpdate to check that it has not flapped back to OK in between.
false_positive_traps: Intentional 'always ALARM' canary or heartbeat alarms; alarms whose ActionsEnabled=false are meant to be dashboard-only.

title: Alarm in INSUFFICIENT_DATA for days (often a deleted resource)
why: The alarm no longer watches anything, so the failure it was built to catch goes unseen.
detect: DescribeAlarms --state-value INSUFFICIENT_DATA with StateUpdatedTimestamp older than 3 days. Confirm with cloudwatch:ListMetrics using the alarm's Namespace, MetricName and Dimensions: no metric returned means the resource is gone or renamed (ListMetrics only covers about the last 2 weeks).
false_positive_traps: Sparse metrics (batch jobs, error counts that emit nothing when there are no errors) are healthy in INSUFFICIENT_DATA. Check TreatMissingData and the metric's emission pattern.

title: Alarm dimensions point at deleted resources
why: Dead alarms give false confidence and cost about $0.10 per alarm-month each.
detect: For each alarm, resolve its dimension (InstanceId, DBInstanceIdentifier, LoadBalancer, FunctionName, QueueName, TableName, ClusterName and so on) with the matching Describe/Get call; NotFound means a zombie alarm. Cheap pre-filter: ListMetrics returns nothing for that dimension set.
api_cost_note: One describe call per resource type; batch where possible.
false_positive_traps: Cross-account or cross-region alarms; metric-math alarms with several metrics; custom namespaces.

title: Alarm with no actions, or actions disabled
why: The alarm fires and nobody is told.
detect: DescribeAlarms: AlarmActions empty (and OKActions/InsufficientDataActions empty), or ActionsEnabled=false. For composite alarms, also check ActionsSuppressor.
false_positive_traps: Child alarms of a composite alarm intentionally have no actions; alarms used only by Auto Scaling or Application Auto Scaling policies show the policy ARN as their action.

title: Alarm action targets a deleted or unsubscribed SNS topic, or the action failed
why: The notification path is silently dead.
detect: For each SNS ARN in AlarmActions, call sns:GetTopicAttributes (NotFound means deleted) and check SubscriptionsConfirmed=0. Also DescribeAlarmHistory --history-item-type Action and look for summaries containing 'Failed to execute action'.
api_cost_note: Free; alarm history is kept for about 30 days.
false_positive_traps: Topics in another account, which you cannot GetTopicAttributes without permission; topics using KMS keys whose policy blocks CloudWatch (that is a real bug, but flag it separately).

title: Subscriptions pending confirmation, or topics with zero confirmed subscriptions
why: Alerts are published into a void.
detect: sns:ListSubscriptionsByTopic: SubscriptionArn == 'PendingConfirmation'. GetTopicAttributes: SubscriptionsConfirmed=0 while SubscriptionsPending>0.
false_positive_traps: Topics consumed only by EventBridge or Lambda through other mechanisms.

title: SNS delivery failures
why: Subscribers (Lambda, SQS, HTTP, SMS) are not receiving messages.
detect: GetMetricData AWS/SNS NumberOfNotificationsFailed (per TopicName), Sum over 24h > 0; compare with NumberOfMessagesPublished. Also check NumberOfNotificationsFilteredOut-InvalidAttributes, NumberOfNotificationsFailedToRedriveToDlq and NumberOfNotificationsRedrivenToDlq.
api_cost_note: GetMetricData costs about $0.01 per 1,000 metrics requested.
false_positive_traps: HTTP endpoints that are expected to be flaky but have retries or a DLQ; deleted subscribers that are still subscribed are a real issue.

title: SMS month-to-date spend near the account spend limit
why: When the monthly SMS spend limit is reached, SMS sending stops silently (OTP and alert texts fail).
detect: GetMetricData AWS/SNS SMSMonthToDateSpentUSD compared with sns:GetSMSAttributes MonthlySpendLimit (or pinpoint-sms-voice-v2 DescribeSpendLimits EnforcedLimit). Flag above 80%.
api_cost_note: Regional; SMS is often sent from us-east-1.
false_positive_traps: Accounts that do not send SMS.

title: Open AWS Health issues affecting the account
why: AWS-side problems (service degradation, an instance on degraded hardware) explain outages and need action.
detect: health:DescribeEvents filter eventStatusCodes=[open], eventTypeCategories=[issue, accountNotification]; then DescribeAffectedEntities. For organizations: DescribeEventsForOrganization. Without the API, the EventBridge source aws.health delivers events to all plans.
api_cost_note: The Health API requires a Business, Enterprise On-Ramp or Enterprise support plan (SubscriptionRequiredException otherwise); global endpoint (us-east-1).
false_positive_traps: Public events not tied to your resources (check affected entities); events that are closed but still listed.

title: Upcoming scheduled changes: EC2 retirement, reboot, maintenance, RDS/ElastiCache maintenance
why: Instances on retiring hardware are stopped or terminated on the scheduled date; instance-store data is lost.
detect: health:DescribeEvents eventTypeCategories=[scheduledChange], eventStatusCodes=[upcoming, open]. Without Business support: ec2:DescribeInstanceStatus --include-all-instances and look for Events[] with Code in instance-retirement, instance-stop, system-reboot, instance-reboot, system-maintenance and NotBefore. Also rds:DescribePendingMaintenanceActions and elasticache:DescribeUpdateActions.
api_cost_note: EC2 and RDS calls are free and regional; the Health API needs a paid support plan.
false_positive_traps: Events marked '[Completed]' or '[Canceled]' in Description; ASG-managed instances that will be replaced anyway.

title: Instance or system status checks failing
why: The instance is unreachable or on impaired hardware, but still running and billing.
detect: ec2:DescribeInstanceStatus --filters Name=instance-status.status,Values=impaired and system-status.status=impaired (plus attached-ebs-status). Metric AWS/EC2 StatusCheckFailed > 0.
false_positive_traps: Instances during boot (status is 'initializing').

title: EBS volume status impaired or I/O disabled
why: I/O is disabled after potential data inconsistency; the application hangs.
detect: ec2:DescribeVolumeStatus: VolumeStatus.Status in (impaired, warning, insufficient-data); Details io-enabled=failed; Events/Actions such as enable-volume-io. CloudWatch AWS/EBS VolumeStalledIOCheck > 0 (Nitro).
false_positive_traps: insufficient-data on volumes attached to stopped instances.

title: DLM snapshot policy in ERROR state
why: Scheduled snapshots stop silently.
detect: dlm:GetLifecyclePolicies, then GetLifecyclePolicy: State=ERROR, StatusMessage. Metric AWS/EBS ResourcesTargeted / SnapshotsCreateFailed > 0.
false_positive_traps: Policies intentionally DISABLED.

title: Stacks in a failed or rollback state
why: Stacks stuck in UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED or ROLLBACK_COMPLETE block all further deploys; *_FAILED means resources are partially applied.
detect: cloudformation:ListStacks --stack-status-filter CREATE_FAILED ROLLBACK_FAILED ROLLBACK_COMPLETE DELETE_FAILED UPDATE_FAILED UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE IMPORT_ROLLBACK_FAILED. Get the failing resource with DescribeStackEvents (ResourceStatusReason). Flag UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE only when it is the latest status and older than N days.
false_positive_traps: UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE is a stable usable state (the last deploy failed but the stack works); CDK bootstrap or nested stacks show the parent status.

title: Stack drift (resources modified outside IaC)
why: The next deploy may revert hotfixes or fail.
detect: Strictly read-only: DescribeStacks, then DriftInformation.StackDriftStatus=DRIFTED and LastCheckTimestamp. DetectStackDrift starts a detection operation (no resource changes, but it is a write-like API call); then DescribeStackResourceDrifts --stack-resource-drift-status-filters MODIFIED DELETED.
api_cost_note: Free; drift detection is throttled (concurrency limits).
false_positive_traps: NOT_CHECKED stacks; properties CloudFormation cannot detect; ASG desired capacity changed by scaling.

title: StackSet instances OUTDATED or failed operations
why: Org-wide guardrails (Config, roles) are missing in some accounts or regions.
detect: ListStackInstances: Status=OUTDATED or StackInstanceStatus.DetailedStatus in (FAILED, INOPERABLE); ListStackSetOperations Status=FAILED.
false_positive_traps: Accounts that were suspended or closed.

title: Lambda error rate, timeouts and throttles
why: Failed invocations mean lost work or user-facing errors.
detect: GetMetricData AWS/Lambda Errors/Invocations > 1-5% over 24h per FunctionName; Throttles > 0; Duration p99 close to the configured Timeout (lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration).
api_cost_note: GetMetricData is paid per metric; batch up to 500 metrics per call.
false_positive_traps: Functions that return handled errors on purpose; very low invocation counts.

title: Asynchronous events dropped, DLQ or destination delivery failures
why: Events are discarded after retries or age expiry and nothing records them.
detect: AWS/Lambda AsyncEventsDropped > 0, AsyncEventAge rising, DeadLetterErrors > 0, DestinationDeliveryFailures > 0. lambda:GetFunctionEventInvokeConfig or GetFunctionConfiguration DeadLetterConfig: no DLQ or OnFailure destination on async-invoked functions.
false_positive_traps: Functions invoked only synchronously (no async metrics).

title: Function State=Failed/Inactive or LastUpdateStatus=Failed
why: The function cannot run (for example after its subnet, ENI or KMS key was deleted) and every invocation fails.
detect: lambda:ListFunctions, then GetFunctionConfiguration: State in (Failed, Inactive) with StateReasonCode, or LastUpdateStatus=Failed with LastUpdateStatusReasonCode.
false_positive_traps: Inactive functions that have been idle for a long time and reactivate on invoke (they are slow, not broken).

title: Event source mapping disabled or reporting a PROBLEM
why: The stream or queue stops being consumed and the backlog grows silently.
detect: lambda:ListEventSourceMappings: State in (Disabled, Disabling) unexpectedly, or LastProcessingResult starts with 'PROBLEM:' (for example function or permission errors). Metrics: IteratorAge rising (Kinesis/DynamoDB), OffsetLag (Kafka).
false_positive_traps: Intentionally disabled mappings.

title: Dead-letter queues containing messages
why: Every DLQ message is a failed unit of work that nobody reprocessed.
detect: For each queue, GetQueueAttributes RedrivePolicy gives the DLQ ARN set. For each DLQ: ApproximateNumberOfMessages > 0, or GetMetricData AWS/SQS ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible > 0 and ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage. ListDeadLetterSourceQueues confirms the relation. Also check queues whose name contains dlq/dead with no source.
api_cost_note: GetQueueAttributes counts as an SQS request (fractions of a cent).
false_positive_traps: DLQs used as intentional parking lots with a known redrive process; Lambda/SNS/EventBridge DLQs are not referenced by any RedrivePolicy.

title: Queue backlog with old messages and no consumers
why: The consumer is dead; messages expire at MessageRetentionPeriod and are lost.
detect: AWS/SQS ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage > 50% of MessageRetentionPeriod, or NumberOfMessagesDeleted=0 while NumberOfMessagesSent>0 over 24h.
false_positive_traps: Delay queues; batch consumers that run daily.

title: Rule target failed invocations or DLQ deliveries
why: Events matched but never reached their target (for example a deleted Lambda or a missing IAM permission).
detect: AWS/Events FailedInvocations > 0 per RuleName; InvocationsFailedToBeSentToDlq > 0; InvocationsSentToDlq > 0. events:ListTargetsByRule: target ARN no longer exists. Disabled rules: ListRules State=DISABLED.
false_positive_traps: Rules disabled on purpose.

title: Scheduler target errors and Pipes in a failed state
why: Cron-like jobs stop running without notice.
detect: AWS/Scheduler TargetErrorCount, InvocationDroppedCount > 0. pipes:ListPipes CurrentState in (CREATE_FAILED, UPDATE_FAILED, START_FAILED, STOP_FAILED) or STOPPED when the desired state is RUNNING.
api_cost_note: Free list calls; metrics are paid.
false_positive_traps: Intentionally stopped pipes.

title: Failed, timed-out or aborted executions
why: Workflows stop mid-way and leave partial state.
detect: AWS/States ExecutionsFailed, ExecutionsTimedOut, ExecutionsAborted > 0 per StateMachineArn; states:ListExecutions --status-filter FAILED (standard workflows) for details; ExecutionThrottled > 0.
false_positive_traps: Workflows that use Fail states for expected business branches.

title: ECS service running below desired count, crash loops or failed deployments
why: Reduced capacity, or a task that never stays up.
detect: ecs:DescribeServices: runningCount < desiredCount for more than 15 minutes; deployments[].rolloutState=FAILED; events[] messages such as 'unable to place a task' or 'is unhealthy'. ListTasks --desired-status STOPPED, then DescribeTasks stoppedReason/stopCode (EssentialContainerExited, TaskFailedToStart) repeating. Container Insights RunningTaskCount.
api_cost_note: Free; DescribeServices takes 10 services per call.
false_positive_traps: Scaling in progress; desiredCount=0 services; stopped tasks are only kept for about an hour.

title: ASG failing to launch instances
why: Capacity cannot recover after failures (bad AMI, missing launch template, insufficient capacity, quota).
detect: autoscaling:DescribeScalingActivities: StatusCode in (Failed, Cancelled) with StatusMessage, in the last 24h. DescribeAutoScalingGroups: count of InService instances < DesiredCapacity; launch template version or AMI no longer exists (ec2:DescribeImages).
false_positive_traps: Transient Spot InsufficientInstanceCapacity that later succeeded.

title: EKS cluster health issues and insights
why: Control-plane problems (deleted subnets or security groups, a KMS key that is disabled) and upgrade blockers.
detect: eks:DescribeCluster: cluster.health.issues[] non-empty; status != ACTIVE. eks:ListInsights with status ERROR or WARNING (categories UPGRADE_READINESS, MISCONFIGURATION), then DescribeInsight.
false_positive_traps: Insights for deprecated APIs that are only used by already-removed clients (the last-seen window is 30 days).

title: Managed node group DEGRADED or with health issues
why: Nodes are not joining or not scaling; the node group is often stuck mid-update.
detect: eks:ListNodegroups, then DescribeNodegroup: status in (DEGRADED, CREATE_FAILED, DELETE_FAILED) or health.issues[] (codes such as AsgInstanceLaunchFailures, NodeCreationFailure, Ec2LaunchTemplateNotFound, InstanceLimitExceeded). eks:ListUpdates/DescribeUpdate status=Failed.
false_positive_traps: Self-managed or Karpenter nodes are not visible here; check in-cluster NotReady nodes via the Kubernetes API.

title: EKS add-on DEGRADED or update failed
why: Broken CNI, CoreDNS or EBS CSI means pod networking, DNS or volumes fail.
detect: eks:ListAddons, then DescribeAddon: status in (DEGRADED, CREATE_FAILED, UPDATE_FAILED) or health.issues[] (for example ConfigurationConflict, InsufficientNumberOfReplicas). Also compare with DescribeAddonVersions for unsupported versions.
false_positive_traps: Self-managed add-ons do not appear.

title: Failed, expired or partial backup, copy and restore jobs
why: You believe you have backups but you do not.
detect: backup:ListBackupJobs --by-state FAILED (also ABORTED, EXPIRED, PARTIAL) --by-created-after now-7d; ListCopyJobs --by-state FAILED; ListRestoreJobs --by-status FAILED. Org view: ListBackupJobSummaries. Metric AWS/Backup NumberOfBackupJobsFailed.
false_positive_traps: A failure followed by a successful retry in the same window; EXPIRED jobs caused by a backup window that is too short (still a real issue).

title: Stateful resources not covered by any backup plan
why: No recovery point exists for a database or volume when it is needed.
detect: Inventory RDS/Aurora/DynamoDB/EFS/EBS/EC2/S3/FSx (Describe/List or resourcegroupstaggingapi:GetResources), then compare with backup:ListProtectedResources (resources with at least one recovery point) and the selections of each plan (ListBackupPlans, ListBackupSelections, GetBackupSelection resources/tag conditions). Also check ListProtectedResources LastBackupTime older than plan frequency x2. Alternatively Config rules *_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN or Backup Audit Manager control 'resources protected by backup plan'.
api_cost_note: Free; Config rule evaluations and Audit Manager are paid.
false_positive_traps: Resources protected by native mechanisms (RDS automated backups, DynamoDB PITR, Aurora cluster snapshots); ephemeral and replica resources.

title: RDS free storage low or instance in storage-full
why: The database goes read-only or stops when storage is full.
detect: AWS/RDS FreeStorageSpace < 10% of rds:DescribeDBInstances AllocatedStorage (or MaxAllocatedStorage when autoscaling is on, which also has a ceiling); DBInstanceStatus in (storage-full, incompatible-parameters, incompatible-network, inaccessible-encryption-credentials, failed). Aurora: FreeLocalStorage.
api_cost_note: Free describe calls; metrics are paid.
false_positive_traps: Storage autoscaling headroom; Aurora cluster volumes grow automatically (FreeStorageSpace is not meaningful there).

title: Replica lag, replication stopped, and recent RDS failure events
why: Stale reads and failed failover readiness.
detect: AWS/RDS ReplicaLag > 300s (AuroraReplicaLag for Aurora); DescribeDBInstances StatusInfos[].Status=error/stopped for read replication. rds:DescribeEvents --duration 10080 with event categories failure, failover, low storage, notification; look for messages such as 'Replication has stopped' or 'Multi-AZ failover'.
api_cost_note: Free; events are kept for 14 days.
false_positive_traps: Lag spikes during large batch writes or backups.

title: Pending maintenance actions with forced apply dates
why: Forced patching or upgrades apply automatically at ForcedApplyDate or AutoAppliedAfterDate.
detect: rds:DescribePendingMaintenanceActions: PendingMaintenanceActionDetails[].ForcedApplyDate / AutoAppliedAfterDate within 30 days.
false_positive_traps: Optional actions without dates.

title: Unhealthy targets and ELB 5xx
why: Users get errors, or the load balancer has no healthy target.
detect: elbv2:DescribeTargetHealth: TargetHealth.State in (unhealthy, unavailable) with Reason; target groups with zero healthy targets. AWS/ApplicationELB HTTPCode_ELB_5XX_Count, HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count, RejectedConnectionCount; NLB UnHealthyHostCount.
api_cost_note: Free describe calls; metrics are paid.
false_positive_traps: Target groups not attached to any listener (zombie, not an error); targets that are 'draining'.

title: ACM certificates failing or ineligible for renewal
why: HTTPS breaks for users on the expiry date.
detect: acm:ListCertificates --certificate-statuses ISSUED, then DescribeCertificate: RenewalSummary.RenewalStatus in (PENDING_VALIDATION, FAILED) with RenewalStatusReason; RenewalEligibility=INELIGIBLE on certificates in use (InUseBy non-empty); DNS validation CNAME missing from the zone (route53:ListResourceRecordSets). ACM attempts managed renewal 60 days before expiry; 'ACM Certificate Approaching Expiration' EventBridge events start 45 days before (configurable via PutAccountConfiguration DaysBeforeExpiry).
api_cost_note: Free; regional (CloudFront certificates are in us-east-1).
false_positive_traps: Unused certificates (InUseBy empty) are expected to be ineligible; email-validated certificates show PENDING_VALIDATION until someone clicks the link.

title: Imported ACM and IAM server certificates near expiry
why: These never auto-renew; expiry causes a hard TLS outage.
detect: acm:DescribeCertificate with Type=IMPORTED: NotAfter < now+30d; CloudWatch AWS/CertificateManager DaysToExpiry. iam:ListServerCertificates Expiration < now+30d (also already expired). Also check certificates in PENDING_VALIDATION for more than 72h (they will time out).
false_positive_traps: Expired certificates not attached to anything (zombie, lower severity).

title: Route 53 health checks failing
why: Failover DNS may be routing away from (or to) a broken endpoint; the endpoint is down.
detect: route53:ListHealthChecks, then GetHealthCheckStatus (HealthCheckObservations[].StatusReport.Status 'Failure'). Metric AWS/Route53 HealthCheckStatus=0 (us-east-1 only), HealthCheckPercentageHealthy.
api_cost_note: Free; metrics are only in us-east-1.
false_positive_traps: Health checks for endpoints that were decommissioned (zombie, still costs $0.50+/month each); Disabled/Inverted health checks.

title: DNSSEC KSK action needed or internal failure
why: If the KMS key behind the KSK becomes inaccessible, ZSK rotation stops and the zone can go SERVFAIL for validating resolvers.
detect: route53:GetDNSSEC --hosted-zone-id: Status.ServeSignature not 'SIGNING' or KeySigningKeys[].Status=ACTION_NEEDED. Metrics AWS/Route53 DNSSECInternalFailure and DNSSECKeySigningKeysNeedingAction > 0 per HostedZoneId. Cross-check the KMS key state (must be Enabled, ECC_NIST_P256, in us-east-1).
false_positive_traps: Zones without DNSSEC.

title: Registered domain near expiry with auto-renew off, or transfer lock off
why: An expired domain takes down every service that uses it.
detect: route53domains:ListDomains (us-east-1): Expiry < now+45d and AutoRenew=false; GetDomainDetail StatusList contains clientTransferProhibited (missing means unlocked).
false_positive_traps: Domains intentionally being let go.

title: CloudFront 5xx error rate
why: Origin failures are reaching users.
detect: AWS/CloudFront 5xxErrorRate (Region=Global, metrics in us-east-1) > 1% per DistributionId; with additional metrics enabled: OriginLatency, 502/503/504 rates. cloudfront:ListDistributions: Enabled=true with an origin domain that does not resolve or a deleted S3 bucket (s3:HeadBucket 404).
api_cost_note: Default metrics are free; additional per-distribution metrics are a paid opt-in.
false_positive_traps: Low-traffic distributions where one error is a large percentage.

title: API Gateway 5xx, integration errors and latency
why: API consumers get errors.
detect: REST: AWS/ApiGateway 5XXError / Count > 1% per ApiName+Stage; IntegrationLatency near the 29s integration timeout. HTTP API: AWS/ApiGateway 5xx (per ApiId). WebSocket: IntegrationError, ExecutionError.
false_positive_traps: 4xx is usually client-caused; do not mix it in.

title: Config recorder stopped, failing, or delivery channel failing
why: There is no change history or compliance data, and Config rules and Security Hub controls stop evaluating.
detect: config:DescribeConfigurationRecorderStatus: recording=false or lastStatus=Failure (lastErrorCode); no recorder in an active region. DescribeDeliveryChannelStatus: configHistoryDeliveryInfo/configSnapshotDeliveryInfo lastStatus=FAILURE. Newer service-linked recorders: ListConfigurationRecorders.
false_positive_traps: Regions blocked by an SCP or opted out; intentionally limited recording scope.

title: Config rules NON_COMPLIANT or evaluation errors
why: Known policy violations or rules that silently stopped evaluating.
detect: config:DescribeComplianceByConfigRule ComplianceType=NON_COMPLIANT; DescribeConfigRuleEvaluationStatus: LastErrorCode present or LastSuccessfulEvaluationTime stale; conformance packs: DescribeConformancePackCompliance.
false_positive_traps: Rules for resource types you do not use.

title: No multi-region trail, trail not logging, or delivery errors
why: There is no audit trail for incidents; delivery errors mean logs are being silently dropped.
detect: cloudtrail:DescribeTrails --include-shadow-trails: no trail with IsMultiRegionTrail=true and IncludeGlobalServiceEvents=true. GetTrailStatus: IsLogging=false, LatestDeliveryError non-empty (for example S3 bucket policy or KMS errors), LatestDeliveryTime stale > 24h. Event data stores (Lake): ListEventDataStores Status.
false_positive_traps: An organization trail owned by the management account shows as a shadow trail in member accounts.

title: GuardDuty off in a region, or high-severity findings unarchived
why: Active compromise indicators (crypto mining, credential exfiltration) are left unattended.
detect: guardduty:ListDetectors empty or GetDetector Status=DISABLED per region. ListFindings with criterion severity >= 7 (High; Critical is 9+), service.archived=false, updatedAt older than 7 days.
api_cost_note: Free reads; GuardDuty itself is paid.
false_positive_traps: Findings already suppressed by filters; pentest findings.

title: Critical or high Security Hub CSPM control failures
why: Aggregated best-practice violations that are left open.
detect: securityhub:GetFindings filters ComplianceStatus=FAILED, RecordState=ACTIVE, WorkflowStatus in (NEW, NOTIFIED), SeverityLabel in (CRITICAL, HIGH). Hub not enabled: DescribeHub error InvalidAccessException.
api_cost_note: Free reads; GetFindings is throttled (about 3 requests per second). Note the 2025 rename: the classic product is now 'Security Hub CSPM'.
false_positive_traps: Controls for unused services; findings duplicated across standards (enable consolidated control findings).

title: Critical or high CVEs with an available fix (Inspector v2)
why: Exploitable vulnerabilities on running compute or images.
detect: inspector2:ListFindings filterCriteria severity=CRITICAL/HIGH, findingStatus=ACTIVE, fixAvailable=YES, exploitAvailable=YES (prioritize), firstObservedAt older than 14d. Coverage gaps: inspector2:ListCoverage scanStatusCode != ACTIVE.
false_positive_traps: ECR images no longer deployed (filter by lastInUseAt / in-use count).

title: Active external-access findings
why: Resources (S3, KMS, IAM roles, secrets, snapshots) are shared outside the zone of trust.
detect: accessanalyzer:ListAnalyzers (type ACCOUNT/ORGANIZATION; none means not enabled), then ListFindingsV2 filter status=ACTIVE, findingType=ExternalAccess. Optional: unused access analyzers (paid) for UnusedIAMRole and similar.
api_cost_note: External-access analyzers are free; unused-access analyzers are paid per role/user.
false_positive_traps: Intentional third-party roles (vendors); archive rules.

title: Publicly accessible S3 buckets
why: Data exposure.
detect: s3control:GetPublicAccessBlock (account) not all four true; per bucket s3:GetBucketPolicyStatus IsPublic=true, GetPublicAccessBlock, GetBucketAcl grants to AllUsers/AuthenticatedUsers.
api_cost_note: Free (S3 control calls are not billed as requests; unverified for every call).
false_positive_traps: Static website buckets fronted intentionally (prefer CloudFront OAC).

title: Security groups open to 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 on 22, 3389 or DB ports
why: Brute-force and data exposure on internet-reachable hosts.
detect: ec2:DescribeSecurityGroupRules: IsEgress=false, CidrIpv4=0.0.0.0/0 or CidrIpv6=::/0, port range covering 22, 3389, 3306, 5432, 1433, 1521, 27017, 6379, 9200, 5439, or IpProtocol=-1. Then check attachment (DescribeNetworkInterfaces filter group-id) to prioritize groups in use.
false_positive_traps: Groups attached only to private-subnet resources without a public IP (still risky, lower priority); bastions behind other controls.

title: Root account has access keys or no MFA
why: Full-account compromise risk.
detect: iam:GetAccountSummary: SummaryMap.AccountAccessKeysPresent=1 or AccountMFAEnabled=0. iam:GenerateCredentialReport + GetCredentialReport row '<root_account>' (password_last_used recent, access_key_1_active). With Organizations centralized root access, member accounts may have no root credentials (that is fine).
api_cost_note: Free; GenerateCredentialReport only generates a report (no resource change).
false_positive_traps: Member accounts managed via centralized root access show no MFA because there is no root password.

title: KMS keys pending deletion or disabled while still in use
why: After the 7-30 day waiting period the key is destroyed and all data encrypted with it is unrecoverable; disabled keys break decrypt now.
detect: kms:ListKeys, then DescribeKey: KeyState in (PendingDeletion, PendingReplicaDeletion, Disabled, Unavailable) with DeletionDate. Usage check: CloudTrail LookupEvents for Decrypt/GenerateDataKey with that key that failed with KMSInvalidStateException; the CloudWatch metric/alarm pattern from the KMS docs.
api_cost_note: Free (DescribeKey counts toward KMS request quotas).
false_positive_traps: Keys actually retired with no remaining ciphertext.

title: Secret rotation enabled but failing or overdue
why: Credentials go stale, or AWSPENDING versions linger and break apps.
detect: secretsmanager:ListSecrets: RotationEnabled=true and LastRotatedDate older than RotationRules interval x1.5 (or NextRotationDate in the past); DescribeSecret VersionIdsToStages shows a stuck AWSPENDING. CloudTrail RotationFailed events.
api_cost_note: Free reads (API calls are billed at $0.05 per 10,000).
false_positive_traps: Secrets whose rotation was just enabled.

title: Usage above 80% of a service quota
why: Launches, deploys or API calls start failing at the limit (vCPU, EIP, ENI, Lambda concurrency and so on).
detect: GetMetricData on AWS/Usage metrics with the metric-math expression m1/SERVICE_QUOTA(m1)*100 > 80. servicequotas:ListServiceQuotas, which returns UsageMetric for each supported quota, plus GetAWSDefaultServiceQuota. Trusted Advisor 'Service Limits' checks as a cross-check.
api_cost_note: Service Quotas reads are free; metric reads are paid; regional.
false_positive_traps: Quotas without a usage metric need a manual count; spiky usage.

title: Budgets exceeded or forecast to exceed
why: Spend has overrun its plan.
detect: budgets:DescribeBudgets: CalculatedSpend.ActualSpend > BudgetLimit, or ForecastedSpend > BudgetLimit; DescribeNotificationsForBudget shows notifications with no subscribers.
false_positive_traps: Budgets with stale limits from an earlier year.

title: Open cost anomalies, or no anomaly monitor
why: Runaway spend (for example a log loop or NAT traffic) is caught days earlier.
detect: ce:GetAnomalies DateInterval last 30d, TotalImpact >= threshold, Feedback unset. ce:GetAnomalyMonitors empty means no monitor; GetAnomalySubscriptions shows subscriptions with no subscribers.
api_cost_note: Cost Explorer API costs $0.01 per request (unverified for anomaly endpoints; assume paid).
false_positive_traps: Planned launches.

title: Savings Plans or RIs expiring within 30-60 days
why: After expiry, usage silently falls back to on-demand rates, often 30-70% more.
detect: savingsplans:DescribeSavingsPlans states=[active], end < now+60d (also queued). ec2:DescribeReservedInstances State=active End < now+60d; rds:DescribeReservedDBInstances, elasticache:DescribeReservedCacheNodes, redshift, opensearch reserved equivalents (StartTime + Duration).
false_positive_traps: Intentionally not renewing because of a migration.

title: Savings Plans or RI utilization below 90%
why: You pay for commitments that you do not use.
detect: ce:GetSavingsPlansUtilization and ce:GetReservationUtilization over the last 30 days: UtilizationPercentage < 90.
false_positive_traps: Seasonal workloads.

title: SES bounce or complaint rate near the review or pause threshold
why: The account goes under review at a 5% bounce or 0.1% complaint rate; sending can be paused at 10% bounce or 0.5% complaint, which stops all email.
detect: sesv2:GetAccount: EnforcementStatus (HEALTHY / PROBATION / SHUTDOWN), SendingEnabled=false, ProductionAccessEnabled. Metrics AWS/SES Reputation.BounceRate > 0.03 and Reputation.ComplaintRate > 0.0005 (alert before review). Also SendQuota SentLast24Hours / Max24HourSend > 80%.
false_positive_traps: Low-volume accounts (rates are computed over a representative volume, not a fixed window).

title: Sending identity no longer verified, or DKIM failing
why: Mail from that domain fails or goes to spam.
detect: sesv2:ListEmailIdentities, then GetEmailIdentity: VerificationStatus != SUCCESS, DkimAttributes.Status in (FAILED, TEMPORARY_FAILURE), MailFromAttributes.MailFromDomainStatus=FAILED.
false_positive_traps: Identities that are no longer used.

title: DynamoDB throttling and system errors
why: Throttled writes and reads become application errors or lost data.
detect: AWS/DynamoDB ThrottledRequests, ReadThrottleEvents, WriteThrottleEvents, SystemErrors > 0 per TableName/GSI; global tables ReplicationLatency high; PITR off: DescribeContinuousBackups PointInTimeRecoveryStatus=DISABLED.
false_positive_traps: Short bursts absorbed by retries.

title: OpenSearch cluster red/yellow, or writes blocked
why: Index writes are rejected (disk or JVM pressure); search fails.
detect: AWS/ES ClusterStatus.red=1 / ClusterStatus.yellow=1, ClusterIndexWritesBlocked=1, FreeStorageSpace low, JVMMemoryPressure > 90, AutomatedSnapshotFailure=1 (dimensions DomainName+ClientId).
false_positive_traps: Yellow on single-node dev domains (replicas cannot be assigned).

title: ElastiCache failover, node replacement and memory pressure
why: Cache evictions or failovers cause latency spikes and errors.
detect: elasticache:DescribeEvents --duration 10080 (messages about failover, node replacement, failed snapshot); metrics Evictions, DatabaseMemoryUsagePercentage > 90, EngineCPUUtilization > 90; DescribeUpdateActions with UpdateActionStatus not-applied and past the recommended apply-by date.
false_positive_traps: Evictions on caches sized as LRU on purpose.

title: Managed nodes ConnectionLost, or patch compliance failing
why: You lose remote access, patching and inventory without noticing.
detect: ssm:DescribeInstanceInformation: PingStatus=ConnectionLost (and LastPingDateTime > 24h); compare with ec2 running instances to find instances that are not managed. ssm:ListComplianceSummaries / DescribeInstancePatchStates FailedCount>0 or MissingCount of critical patches; ListCommandInvocations Status=Failed for maintenance windows.
false_positive_traps: Stopped instances show ConnectionLost.

title: VPN tunnels down or Direct Connect connections not available
why: Hybrid connectivity has lost its redundancy, or has failed entirely.
detect: ec2:DescribeVpnConnections: VgwTelemetry[].Status=DOWN (alert when either tunnel is DOWN; both DOWN is an outage). AWS/VPN TunnelState=0. directconnect:DescribeConnections connectionState not 'available'; DescribeVirtualInterfaces bgpPeers[].bgpStatus=down.
false_positive_traps: Intentional single-tunnel customer gateways.

title: NAT gateway port allocation errors or dropped packets
why: Outbound connections from private subnets fail intermittently.
detect: AWS/NATGateway ErrorPortAllocation > 0, PacketsDropCount > 0 (sustained); ec2:DescribeNatGateways State=failed (FailureCode).
false_positive_traps: Brief drops during deploys.

title: Canaries failing, or stopped and no longer running
why: The external user-journey check is broken, or nothing is watching.
detect: synthetics:DescribeCanaries: Status.State in (ERROR, STOPPED) when it should be RUNNING; DescribeCanariesLastRun LastRun.Status.State=FAILED; AWS/CloudWatchSynthetics SuccessPercent < 100. Runtime version deprecated: compare RuntimeVersion with DescribeRuntimeVersions DeprecationDate.
false_positive_traps: Canaries intentionally stopped.

title: Firehose delivery failing, or Kinesis consumers lagging
why: Logs and analytics data are lost or delayed.
detect: AWS/Firehose DeliveryToS3.Success < 1 (also Redshift/OpenSearch/HttpEndpoint DeliveryTo*.Success), DeliveryToS3.DataFreshness rising; failed records in the S3 error prefix. Kinesis: GetRecords.IteratorAgeMilliseconds high, WriteProvisionedThroughputExceeded > 0.
false_positive_traps: Buffering intervals inflate DataFreshness.

title: Recurring job and pipeline failures
why: ETL, batch jobs and deploys are failing silently.
detect: glue:GetJobRuns JobRunState in (FAILED, TIMEOUT, ERROR) in the last 7 days; batch:ListJobs jobStatus=FAILED per queue, and DescribeComputeEnvironments status=INVALID; codepipeline:ListPipelineExecutions status=Failed as the latest; codebuild:ListBuildsForProject + BatchGetBuilds buildStatus=FAILED streaks.
false_positive_traps: Feature-branch pipelines.

title: Beanstalk environment health Red/Degraded
why: The application is serving errors.
detect: elasticbeanstalk:DescribeEnvironments: Health in (Red, Yellow) or HealthStatus in (Degraded, Severe); DescribeEvents Severity=ERROR.
false_positive_traps: Environments mid-deploy.

title: Trusted Advisor checks in error (red) status
why: A broad cross-check that catches items not covered elsewhere (limits, exposed keys, fault tolerance).
detect: trustedadvisor:ListRecommendations status=error/warning (global API); ListRecommendationResources for affected resources. The legacy support:DescribeTrustedAdvisorCheckResult is an alternative.
api_cost_note: Requires Business, Enterprise On-Ramp or Enterprise support for full checks and the API (unverified for the new trustedadvisor API on Basic).
false_positive_traps: Duplicates the dedicated checks above; de-duplicate by resource ARN.

title: Critical log groups stopped receiving events
why: Agents or log shipping are broken, so monitoring is blind.
detect: logs:DescribeLogGroups, then DescribeLogStreams --order-by LastEventTime --descending --limit 1: lastIngestionTime older than the expected interval for groups that had recent traffic; AWS/Logs IncomingLogEvents=0 per LogGroupName. Subscription filters to deleted destinations: DescribeSubscriptionFilters destinationArn missing.
api_cost_note: DescribeLogStreams is throttled (about 25 TPS); lastEventTimestamp updates are eventually consistent.
false_positive_traps: Log groups of deleted resources (zombie, not an error).

title: Principals with an AWSCompromisedKeyQuarantine policy attached, or an exposed-credentials Health event
why: AWS detected a leaked access key and quarantined it. The key is still partly usable and the leak source is still open, and AWS opens a support case that expects action.
detect: iam:ListEntitiesForPolicy for arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AWSCompromisedKeyQuarantine, ...V2 and ...V3; health:DescribeEvents with eventTypeCodes AWS_RISK_CREDENTIALS_EXPOSED and AWS_RISK_IAM_QUARANTINE (sources disagree on the code, so match both); Trusted Advisor 'Exposed Access Keys'
false_positive_traps: A detached policy can still leave an active key behind, so also check the key's status. Some reports name the event AWS_RISK_IAM_QUARANTINE.
api_cost_note: Free. IAM calls are global. Health needs Business support or higher for the API (see the support-plan check).

title: Open AWS abuse reports (AWS_ABUSE_* events) against account resources
why: An unanswered abuse report (DoS, spam, phishing hosted on your IPs) can end in resource blocking or account suspension. It usually means a compromised instance.
detect: health:DescribeEvents filter eventTypeCodes starting AWS_ABUSE_ (for example AWS_ABUSE_DOS_REPORT), statusCodes open; DescribeAffectedEntities to get the instance or IP
false_positive_traps: Reports about IPs that were already released. Confirm current ownership of the EIP or ENI.
api_cost_note: Health API needs Business support or higher. Global endpoint is us-east-1.
source: https://github.com/aws/aws-health-tools (event code list; exact codes unverified in this run)

title: Roles trusting a CI OIDC provider with no or a wildcard 'sub' condition
why: A role that trusts token.actions.githubusercontent.com (or GitLab, Terraform Cloud and similar) without a repo-scoped sub condition can be assumed by any repository on that platform.
detect: iam:ListRoles; parse AssumeRolePolicyDocument for Principal.Federated pointing at an OIDC provider; flag when there is no Condition on <provider>:sub, or the sub value is '*' or 'repo:*' or has an org-wide wildcard; iam:ListOpenIDConnectProviders to map providers
false_positive_traps: Repo-wide 'repo:org/repo:*' is broad but intentional. Also accept GitHub's new immutable-ID sub format (repos created after 2026-07-15).

title: Instances, launch templates or Region defaults that still allow IMDSv1
why: IMDSv1 lets SSRF bugs steal instance-role credentials, and the account default does not change existing instances.
detect: ec2:DescribeInstances MetadataOptions.HttpTokens=optional; ec2:DescribeLaunchTemplateVersions MetadataOptions; ec2:GetInstanceMetadataDefaults per Region (HttpTokens, HttpTokensEnforced); CloudWatch MetadataNoToken>0 shows IMDSv1 is actually in use
false_positive_traps: Old agents or SDKs that need v1. Use MetadataNoToken to separate 'allowed' from 'used'.

title: Publicly shared EBS snapshots, AMIs, RDS snapshots or SSM documents, and block-public-access turned off
why: Public snapshots and AMIs often leak whole disks with secrets and data, and anyone can copy them.
detect: ec2:DescribeSnapshots --owner-ids self --restorable-by-user-ids all; ec2:DescribeImages --owners self Public=true; ec2:GetSnapshotBlockPublicAccessState and ec2:GetImageBlockPublicAccessState (AMI API name unverified in this run); rds:DescribeDBSnapshotAttributes and DescribeDBClusterSnapshotAttributes where restore includes 'all'; ssm:DescribeDocumentPermission AccountIds contains 'all'
false_positive_traps: Intentionally public AMIs from a publisher account. State 'block-new-sharing' still leaves existing public snapshots public.
api_cost_note: Free. Per Region, and many snapshots means pagination.

title: EBS encryption-by-default disabled in a Region
why: New volumes and snapshot copies are created unencrypted unless every caller remembers to ask for encryption.
detect: ec2:GetEbsEncryptionByDefault per enabled Region; ec2:GetEbsDefaultKmsKeyId to confirm the key still exists and is enabled
false_positive_traps: Regions that are intentionally unused. Combine with the unexpected-regions inventory.

title: IAM users with a console password and no MFA
why: A password-only console login is the most common takeover path, and the root-only check misses these users.
detect: iam:GenerateCredentialReport then GetCredentialReport; rows with password_enabled=true and mfa_active=false; also iam:GetAccountPasswordPolicy (missing or weak)
false_positive_traps: Break-glass users that have a hardware MFA registered as a virtual device are still reported correctly. Federated users don't appear here.
api_cost_note: Free. The report can be up to 4 hours old.

title: Trust, key or bucket policies that reference deleted principals (unique IDs instead of ARNs)
why: When a referenced principal is deleted, its ARN is replaced by an AROA/AIDA unique ID, so access breaks silently and recreating the principal does not restore it.
detect: Scan role trust policies (iam:ListRoles), kms:GetKeyPolicy, s3:GetBucketPolicy, sqs/sns/lambda resource policies for Principal values matching ^(AROA|AIDA|AGPA)[A-Z0-9]+$
false_positive_traps: None significant. A unique ID in a Principal element means the principal was deleted.
api_cost_note: Free. Bucket and key policies are per Region.

title: SAML identity provider metadata or signing certificate expiring
why: When the IdP signing certificate or the provider's ValidUntil date passes, every federated console and CLI login fails at once.
detect: iam:ListSAMLProviders ValidUntil; iam:GetSAMLProvider and parse SAMLMetadataDocument X509 notAfter (<30 days); for Identity Center, check the external IdP certificate expiry in the console (no public API, unverified)
false_positive_traps: Unused providers. Cross-check with the iam-orphan-policies-providers-certs check.

title: Function URLs with AuthType NONE, or resource policies allowing Principal '*'
why: Anyone on the internet can invoke the function, which exposes data or runs up cost.
detect: lambda:ListFunctions then ListFunctionUrlConfigs (AuthType=NONE); lambda:GetPolicy where Principal '*' or Service principal has no aws:SourceArn or aws:SourceAccount condition
false_positive_traps: Intentional public webhooks that validate a signature in code. Report them as info with an owner tag.
api_cost_note: Free. Per Region, one call per function.

title: Secrets stored in plaintext env vars, user data, build env or stack parameters
why: Anyone with read-only Describe permissions, and CloudTrail or console viewers, can read the credentials.
detect: lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration Environment; ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition containerDefinitions[].environment; ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute userData (base64); codebuild:BatchGetProjects environmentVariables type PLAINTEXT; cloudformation:DescribeStacks Parameters without NoEcho; regex on names (PASSWORD|SECRET|TOKEN|KEY) plus an entropy test
false_positive_traps: Names like TOKEN_URL or KEY_PREFIX. Never print the values; report only the names and resources.
api_cost_note: Free. Treat the output as sensitive.

title: EKS API endpoint public to 0.0.0.0/0
why: The Kubernetes API is exposed to internet scanning and credential-stuffing, and a single leaked kubeconfig is enough.
detect: eks:DescribeCluster resourcesVpcConfig.endpointPublicAccess=true and publicAccessCidrs contains 0.0.0.0/0
false_positive_traps: Clusters reached by CI runners with dynamic IPs. Suggest an allowlist or private access instead.

title: EKS cluster still authenticating through the deprecated aws-auth ConfigMap
why: aws-auth is deprecated, not audited in CloudTrail, and one bad edit locks everyone out of the cluster.
detect: eks:DescribeCluster accessConfig.authenticationMode in (CONFIG_MAP, API_AND_CONFIG_MAP); eks:ListAccessEntries count
false_positive_traps: API_AND_CONFIG_MAP during an active migration. Moving to API can't be reversed.

title: Load balancers, volumes, security groups and instances tagged for a Kubernetes cluster that no longer exists
why: Deleting a cluster without removing Services, PVCs or Karpenter nodes first leaves billed ELBs, EBS volumes and EC2 instances behind.
detect: resourcegroupstaggingapi:GetResources with TagFilters key prefix kubernetes.io/cluster/, elbv2.k8s.aws/cluster, eks:cluster-name, karpenter.sh/discovery or karpenter.k8s.aws/cluster; compare the cluster names with eks:ListClusters
false_positive_traps: Self-managed (non-EKS) clusters that use the same tags. Check for live nodes before flagging.
api_cost_note: Free. The Tagging API is per Region.

title: Resources left behind by deleted stacks (DeletionPolicy Retain or Snapshot)
why: Buckets, tables, log groups, KMS keys and final snapshots outlive their stack, no IaC owns them, and they keep billing.
detect: cloudformation:ListStacks StackStatusFilter=DELETE_COMPLETE; resourcegroupstaggingapi:GetResources with tag aws:cloudformation:stack-id matching those deleted stack IDs; rds:DescribeDBSnapshots for final snapshots named after those stacks
false_positive_traps: Data kept on purpose for compliance. Flag them for an owner decision rather than deletion.
api_cost_note: Free. ListStacks keeps deleted stacks for 90 days only.

title: Spend and resources with no owner or cost-center tag, or cost allocation tags not activated
why: Untagged spend has nobody to ask about it, so zombie findings can't be routed to an owner.
detect: resourcegroupstaggingapi:GetResources and count resources missing the owner key; ce:GetCostAndUsage GroupBy TAG:<owner> to find the share of spend with an empty value; ce:ListCostAllocationTags Status=Inactive for the owner key
false_positive_traps: Some services can't be tagged, and some line items such as support and tax have no tag.
api_cost_note: Cost Explorer API costs $0.01 per request.

title: Security, billing or operations alternate contacts not set
why: AWS sends deprecation, abuse and billing notices to these contacts. When they are missing, deadlines in this catalog reach only the root email, which nobody may read.
detect: account:GetAlternateContact for AlternateContactType SECURITY, BILLING and OPERATIONS (a ResourceNotFoundException means it is missing); account:GetContactInformation; for org members, call with AccountId from the management or delegated-admin account
false_positive_traps: Contacts that point at a departed person's mailbox. The API can't verify that.
api_cost_note: Free. Org-wide calls need trusted access for Account Management.

title: Route table entries in blackhole state
why: A route that points at a deleted NAT gateway, ENI, peering connection or TGW attachment silently drops traffic for its CIDR.
detect: ec2:DescribeRouteTables Routes[].State=blackhole; ec2:SearchTransitGatewayRoutes with filter state=blackhole for each TGW route table
false_positive_traps: Intentional blackhole routes used to block a CIDR in a TGW.

title: Subnets close to running out of free IP addresses
why: EKS pods, Lambda ENIs, ASG scale-out and RDS failover fail with InsufficientFreeAddresses during a scale event.
detect: ec2:DescribeSubnets AvailableIpAddressCount / (2^(32-prefix)-5) < 15%; weight subnets used by EKS node groups, Lambda VpcConfig or ASGs
false_positive_traps: Tiny dedicated subnets such as TGW /28 attachments that are full by design.

title: Security group rules referencing groups in a deleted peering or VPC
why: Stale rules no longer allow the traffic they were written for, which causes a silent outage after a peering change.
detect: ec2:DescribeStaleSecurityGroups per VPC (returns StaleIpPermissions and StaleIpPermissionsEgress)
false_positive_traps: Only covers peering references. Rules pointing at deleted prefix lists are caught elsewhere.

title: S3 or DynamoDB traffic going through a NAT gateway with no gateway endpoint
why: Every GB to S3 or DynamoDB pays NAT data-processing charges that a free gateway endpoint removes. On data-heavy workloads this is often thousands of dollars a month.
detect: ec2:DescribeNatGateways and ec2:DescribeRouteTables for private route tables with 0.0.0.0/0 to a NAT; ec2:DescribeVpcEndpoints VpcEndpointType=Gateway for com.amazonaws.<region>.s3 and dynamodb missing or not associated with those route tables; CloudWatch NAT BytesOutToDestination; CUR usage type NatGateway-Bytes
false_positive_traps: Cross-Region S3 access doesn't benefit from a gateway endpoint. Endpoint policies can block buckets.
api_cost_note: Free (CloudWatch GetMetricData is billed per metric).

title: Fast Snapshot Restore left enabled
why: Billed at $0.75 per DSU-hour for each snapshot in each AZ (us-east-1), about $540 a month per snapshot-AZ, whether or not anything restores.
detect: ec2:DescribeFastSnapshotRestores State in (enabling, optimizing, enabled); join with recent CreateVolume events from those snapshots in CloudTrail
false_positive_traps: DR runbooks that need FSR on purpose. Confirm with the owner.
api_cost_note: Free. Per Region, max 5 FSR snapshots per Region by default.

title: Recycle Bin retention rules holding deleted snapshots and AMIs
why: Deleted snapshots stay billed at the normal snapshot rate for the whole retention period, so cleanups don't reduce the bill.
detect: rbin:ListRules (ResourceType EBS_SNAPSHOT or EC2_IMAGE, RetentionPeriod); ec2:ListSnapshotsInRecycleBin and ListImagesInRecycleBin; sum the snapshot sizes
false_positive_traps: Intentional ransomware protection. Report the size and cost, not a delete action.

title: Burstable resources running out of credits (T instances, gp2/st1/sc1, EFS bursting, RDS)
why: When credits hit zero the resource is throttled to baseline, which looks like a slow app with no error.
detect: CloudWatch: EC2 CPUCreditBalance near 0 in standard mode; EBS BurstBalance < 20%; EFS BurstCreditBalance trending to 0 with ThroughputMode=bursting; RDS BurstBalance and CPUCreditBalance; for T unlimited, CPUSurplusCreditsCharged > 0 means extra cost instead
false_positive_traps: Short spikes during a nightly batch. Use a sustained window of 1 hour or more.
api_cost_note: GetMetricData is billed per metric requested.

title: Managed databases and caches on previous-generation node classes
why: Old classes (m4/r4/t2 and older) cost more per unit and get forced upgrades. RDS already auto-upgraded db.m4, db.r4 and db.t2 for several engines.
detect: rds:DescribeDBInstances DBInstanceClass matching db.(m1|m2|m3|m4|r3|r4|t2); elasticache:DescribeCacheClusters CacheNodeType cache.(t2|m3|m4|r3|r4); opensearch:DescribeDomains InstanceType (m3|m4|r3|r4|t2|i2|c4); mq:DescribeBroker HostInstanceType mq.(t2|m4); docdb and neptune DescribeDBInstances
false_positive_traps: Reserved nodes still running on the old class. Upgrade when the RI expires.

title: RDS instances on gp2 or io1 storage
why: gp3 gives baseline IOPS independent of size at a lower $/GB, and io2 beats io1. The EBS gp2 check does not see RDS storage.
detect: rds:DescribeDBInstances StorageType in (gp2, io1, standard)
false_positive_traps: Aurora has no StorageType of this kind. Changing storage can trigger a long storage-optimization period.

title: Aurora cluster on the wrong storage configuration (Standard vs I/O-Optimized)
why: AWS guidance is that I/O-Optimized saves up to 40% when I/O is 25% or more of Aurora spend, and Standard is cheaper below that.
detect: rds:DescribeDBClusters StorageType (aurora vs aurora-iopt1); ce:GetCostAndUsage per cluster usage types *Aurora:StorageIOUsage vs instance and storage usage; flag Standard with I/O share >=25%, or iopt1 with I/O share <10%
false_positive_traps: Moving to I/O-Optimized is allowed once every 30 days. Seasonal I/O patterns.
api_cost_note: CE API costs $0.01 per request. Resource-level CE data needs opt-in.

title: Old blue environments left running after a Blue/Green switchover
why: After a switchover, the old instances are renamed -oldN and keep running at full price.
detect: rds:DescribeBlueGreenDeployments Status=SWITCHOVER_COMPLETED; rds:DescribeDBInstances and DescribeDBClusters with identifiers matching -old[0-9]+$; CloudWatch DatabaseConnections≈0
false_positive_traps: Kept for a short rollback window. Flag after 7 days or more.

title: Parameter or option group changes stuck in pending-reboot
why: Security or performance settings that people believe are applied are not, and a surprise reboot later applies them all at once.
detect: rds:DescribeDBInstances DBParameterGroups[].ParameterApplyStatus=pending-reboot, OptionGroupMemberships[].Status; DBClusterMembers[].DBClusterParameterGroupStatus=pending-reboot
false_positive_traps: Changes waiting for a planned maintenance window.

title: RDS Proxies with no client connections, or with unavailable targets
why: Proxies are billed per vCPU of the underlying database every hour. An unhealthy target silently breaks the apps that use the proxy.
detect: rds:DescribeDBProxies; CloudWatch ClientConnections and DatabaseConnections max=0 over 14 days; rds:DescribeDBProxyTargets TargetHealth.State != AVAILABLE
false_positive_traps: Proxies used only during failover tests.

title: Instances that relied on paid Performance Insights retention after the PI console end of life
why: AWS docs give 2026-06-30, and some pages 2026-07-31, for the PI console and flexible retention end. Instances not moved to Advanced mode may have fallen to 7-day history and lost execution plans.
detect: rds:DescribeDBInstances PerformanceInsightsEnabled, PerformanceInsightsRetentionPeriod, DatabaseInsightsMode (standard vs advanced); flag where retention >7 was configured but the mode is standard
false_positive_traps: AWS pages disagree on whether flexible retention is kept in Standard mode. Verify per account.

title: Production tables or databases without deletion protection, PITR or automated backups
why: One mistaken delete or a bad write becomes unrecoverable data loss, and backup plans don't cover deletes inside the PITR window.
detect: dynamodb:DescribeTable DeletionProtectionEnabled=false; dynamodb:DescribeContinuousBackups PointInTimeRecoveryStatus=DISABLED; rds:DescribeDBInstances and DescribeDBClusters DeletionProtection=false, BackupRetentionPeriod=0
false_positive_traps: Ephemeral or test tables. Scope by tag or name.

title: Global tables still on version 2017.11.29 (Legacy)
why: Legacy global tables use more write capacity, emit two stream records per write and support fewer Regions. AWS recommends upgrading to 2019.11.21.
detect: dynamodb:ListGlobalTables (lists only legacy-version tables); dynamodb:DescribeTable GlobalTableVersion
false_positive_traps: Stream consumers that depend on the double records need a review before the upgrade.

title: S3 replication failing, or targeting a deleted bucket or role
why: DR or compliance copies silently stop while the source keeps accepting writes.
detect: s3:GetBucketReplication (check the destination bucket exists and the role exists); CloudWatch AWS/S3 OperationsFailedReplication > 0 and ReplicationLatency (needs replication metrics or RTC); S3 Event Notifications s3:Replication:OperationFailedReplication
false_positive_traps: Objects excluded by filter or KMS permissions show up as failures that are expected.
api_cost_note: Replication metrics are billed as custom metrics.

title: Buckets with ACLs enabled, or object ACL grants to other accounts, AuthenticatedUsers or AllUsers
why: ACL grants get around bucket policies and are invisible in most reviews. BucketOwnerEnforced is the recommended default.
detect: s3:GetBucketOwnershipControls ObjectOwnership != BucketOwnerEnforced; s3:GetBucketAcl grants to non-owner canonical IDs or the URIs .../global/AllUsers and AuthenticatedUsers; s3control:GetPublicAccessBlock at account level
false_positive_traps: Legacy log-delivery ACLs for CloudFront and S3 server access logs.

title: Large EFS file systems with no IA lifecycle, or with unused provisioned throughput
why: Cold data stays on Standard at a much higher $/GB, and provisioned throughput is billed whether used or not.
detect: efs:DescribeFileSystems SizeInBytes.ValueInStandard large; efs:DescribeLifecycleConfiguration empty; ThroughputMode=provisioned with CloudWatch MeteredIOBytes far below ProvisionedThroughputInMibps
false_positive_traps: Latency-sensitive hot data. The first read from IA costs more.

title: Distributions using Dedicated IP custom SSL (SSLSupportMethod=vip)
why: Costs $600 a month per certificate, prorated by the hour, where SNI is free. It is rarely needed today.
detect: cloudfront:ListDistributions ViewerCertificate.SSLSupportMethod=vip
false_positive_traps: A real need to support very old non-SNI clients.

title: S3 origins on legacy Origin Access Identity (OAI) instead of OAC
why: OAI is legacy. It doesn't support SSE-KMS, newer Regions or all S3 methods, so migration is required for those features.
detect: cloudfront:ListCloudFrontOriginAccessIdentities; ListDistributions Origins[].S3OriginConfig.OriginAccessIdentity non-empty and OriginAccessControlId empty; also DefaultCacheBehavior.ForwardedValues (legacy cache settings)
false_positive_traps: None. This is a planned migration.

title: Classic Load Balancers still in use
why: CLB is previous generation, gets no new features or TLS policy improvements, and blocks a move to modern instance families.
detect: elb:DescribeLoadBalancers (v2012 API) non-empty per Region; CloudWatch RequestCount to tell live ones from idle ones
false_positive_traps: Beanstalk legacy environments create CLBs. Migrate through an environment swap.

title: Shield Advanced subscription active or auto-renewing
why: $3,000 a month with a 1-year commitment that auto-renews each year. People often forget it after a trial or incident.
detect: shield:DescribeSubscription (StartTime, EndTime, AutoRenew, TimeCommitmentInSeconds); shield:ListProtections count
false_positive_traps: Billed once per payer or organization. Don't count it per account.

title: WAF web ACLs and rule groups not associated with any resource
why: Each web ACL and rule is billed monthly (about $5 per ACL plus $1 per rule, unverified) while protecting nothing, or a protected resource was detached by mistake.
detect: wafv2:ListWebACLs Scope=REGIONAL per Region and Scope=CLOUDFRONT in us-east-1; wafv2:ListResourcesForWebACL empty; cloudfront:ListDistributionsByWebACLId empty
false_positive_traps: Firewall Manager-managed ACLs waiting for new resources.

title: API Gateway stage caches and AppSync caches billed hourly with low hit rates
why: Cache clusters bill every hour regardless of traffic, and they often get enabled for a test and forgotten.
detect: apigateway:GetStages cacheClusterEnabled=true, cacheClusterSize; CloudWatch CacheHitCount vs CacheMissCount; appsync:GetApiCache type and status
false_positive_traps: Caches protecting a fragile backend, where a low hit rate is still worth it.

title: AppSync API keys and API Gateway client certificates near expiry
why: AppSync keys last at most 365 days (default 7) and API Gateway client certificates last 365 days. When they expire, client or backend auth fails abruptly.
detect: appsync:ListGraphqlApis then ListApiKeys 'expires' < now+30d; apigateway:GetClientCertificates expirationDate < now+30d; apigateway:GetDomainNames MutualTlsAuthentication.TruststoreWarnings
false_positive_traps: Unused keys on dead APIs. Join with request metrics.

title: KMS keys whose imported key material expires soon or already expired
why: When it expires, KMS deletes the material and the key goes to PendingImport, so every decrypt using it fails until the same material is reimported.
detect: kms:ListKeys then DescribeKey where Origin=EXTERNAL and ExpirationModel=KEY_MATERIAL_EXPIRES and ValidTo < now+30d, or KeyState=PendingImport
false_positive_traps: Keys intentionally left to expire as crypto-shredding.
api_cost_note: Free (KMS API request pricing applies at high volume).

title: User pool Lambda triggers pointing at deleted or unauthorized functions
why: Sign-up, sign-in or token generation fails for every user once the trigger function is gone or loses invoke permission.
detect: cognito-idp:ListUserPools then DescribeUserPool LambdaConfig ARNs; lambda:GetFunction (ResourceNotFound) and lambda:GetPolicy missing the cognito-idp.amazonaws.com principal
false_positive_traps: Triggers referencing a specific version or alias that exists.
api_cost_note: Free. Cognito has low TPS quotas, so throttle the calls.

title: Identity pools allowing unauthenticated identities with a broad IAM role
why: Anyone can get AWS credentials from a public identity pool ID, which is often embedded in mobile or web apps.
detect: cognito-identity:ListIdentityPools then DescribeIdentityPool AllowUnauthenticatedIdentities=true; GetIdentityPoolRoles unauthenticated role, then IAM policy analysis for wildcard actions or resources
false_positive_traps: Narrow unauth roles, for example only Pinpoint putEvents, are by design.

title: Source connections in PENDING or ERROR state
why: Pipelines and other tools using the connection can't pull source, so deploys silently stop.
detect: codeconnections:ListConnections (and the legacy codestar-connections:ListConnections) ConnectionStatus in (PENDING, ERROR); join with codepipeline:GetPipeline source actions that use the ConnectionArn
false_positive_traps: Connections created and never used.

title: Workloads invoking Bedrock models in Legacy state or past public extended access
why: Legacy models reach end of life at least 6 months after entering Legacy. The extended-access phase charges higher prices, and after EOL calls fail.
detect: bedrock:ListFoundationModels per Region modelLifecycle.status=LEGACY (also check publicExtendedAccessTime and EOL fields); join with CloudWatch AWS/Bedrock Invocations by ModelId, bedrock:ListInferenceProfiles, bedrock-agent:GetAgent foundationModel, knowledge base embeddingModelArn, ListProvisionedModelThroughputs modelArn
false_positive_traps: Lifecycle can differ by Region. The API enum has only ACTIVE and LEGACY, while the user guide also lists EOL.

title: Always-on AI service endpoints with no traffic
why: These bill until deleted or stopped. Comprehend charges $0.0005 per second per IU (about $1.80/hr), Rekognition Custom Labels about $4 per inference hour, and a Kendra index is billed while it exists.
detect: comprehend:ListEndpoints (Status IN_SERVICE, CurrentInferenceUnits); rekognition:DescribeProjects then DescribeProjectVersions Status=RUNNING; kendra:ListIndices; personalize:ListCampaigns then DescribeCampaign minProvisionedTPS; rekognition:ListStreamProcessors RUNNING; CloudWatch invocation and query metrics = 0 over 14 days
false_positive_traps: Low-volume but critical classifiers. Check the owner tag.

title: Canvas sessions, MLflow tracking servers, HyperPod clusters and training warm pools left running
why: A Canvas workspace bills about $1.90/hr until logout, and tracking servers, HyperPod nodes and warm pools bill hourly. The existing endpoint, notebook and Studio checks miss these.
detect: sagemaker:ListApps AppType=Canvas Status=InService; sagemaker:ListMlflowTrackingServers IsActive; sagemaker:ListClusters (HyperPod) InService; sagemaker:ListTrainingJobs WarmPoolStatus.Status=Available; sagemaker:ListInferenceComponents with 0 invocations
false_positive_traps: Long-running HyperPod reservations that are intentional.

title: Paid per-user AI seats with no activity
why: Q Developer Pro costs $19 per user per month and Q Business $3 or $20, billed for the full month even if cancelled mid-month.
detect: qbusiness:ListApplications then ListSubscriptions; Q Developer subscription list and usage through the Q Developer dashboard or user-activity reports (API unverified); CE SERVICE='Amazon Q' by usage type
false_positive_traps: New hires who haven't onboarded yet.
